Voyager 1 Beat the Odds and Is Still Working a Light-Day Away From Earth

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (841 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • One of NASA’s longest-tenured spacecraft is quite literally stuck in the past.
  • In a recent development, voyager 1, debuted in September 1977 toward the outer planets of our solar system, achieved a historic milestone on Wednesday: It became the first human-made object to reach one light-day from Earth.
  • Sources indicate that “It's just a wonderful happenstance,” Kareem Badaruddin, Voyager mission manager at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory, says of the milestone.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One of NASA’s longest-tenured spacecraft is quite literally stuck in the past.

In a recent development, voyager 1, debuted in September 1977 toward the outer planets of our solar system, achieved a historic milestone on Wednesday: It became the first human-made object to reach one light-day from Earth. The spacecraft is so far away, that by the time its light reaches Earth, it comes from the spacecraft as it existed one day in the past. The achievement is one researchers hadn’t planned on, and yet, as Voyager 1 wades deeper into uncharted stretches of the galaxy, it continues sending back valuable scientific information.

Sources indicate that “It's just a wonderful happenstance,” Kareem Badaruddin, Voyager mission manager at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory, says of the milestone. “Just as the stars were aligned for the tour of the planets, they're also aligned for this really magical, special thing that's happening for humankind.”.

Industry observers note that for Fran Bagenal, a planetary scientist at the University of Colorado, Boulder, who began working with Voyager 1 as a graduate student during its earliest years, the occasion is a momentous technological feat. “What's exciting is the fact that we have a spacecraft that was built in the mid ’70s that is still working,” she says. “Storing data on an eight-track tape that’s working on a spacecraft after 50 years—I mean, it’s amazing.”.

Recent findings suggest that even as Voyager 1 approaches its 50-year anniversary next September, and its end of mission perhaps not long after that, the spacecraft is still checking items off its laundry list of scientific achievements. The spacecraft—alongside its twin, Voyager 2—was originally intended to take advantage of a rare planetary alignment to observe the outer planets.

But Voyager 1 kept traveling beyond the solar system and is now exploring the interstellar medium that fills the space between star systems. Voyager 1’s remoteness gives researchers a rare opportunity to study how the effects of the sun ripple even into the interstellar medium—and at what point those effects wane, indicates Jamie Rankin, deputy project scientist for the Voyager Mission at Princeton University.

According to recent reports, just as both Voyager spacecraft are moving through space, so is our own solar system—only about 35,000 miles per hour slower, Badaruddin says. That means that as the pair continue their journeys, they’re sending back information about the space that our own sun and planet will pass through in about three years’ time.

“We can learn from telescopes and Earth-orbiting observatories, but there's really nothing like having a spacecraft in that environment that's sending us data,” Badaruddin says.

Recent findings suggest that voyager 1’s unprecedented journey isn’t without challenges. The craft has stayed in communication with Earth far longer than planned and is trekking through regions of space that it was never built to encounter or study. Researchers are helping maintain crucial functions, but they’re now doing so with a full day of lag in communications both to and from the spacecraft, Badaruddin says.

“Light time is really affecting us,” he says. “You factor it in. It’s like having a long commute.” Building latest commands for the spacecraft is now a week-long process, for instance, since it takes time to receive data from the spacecraft, analyze it, and create a new command, he adds.

Still, the Voyager team is used to navigating unforeseen circumstances. For decades, they’ve been managing to make do with a dwindling power supply coming from the craft’s nuclear generators. In September, mission operations switched off some of Voyager 1’s devices in lieu of lower-power alternatives, a maneuver the team dubbed the “Big Bang.” The swap, which saved the craft 10 watts of power, kept mission operations from having to switch off another instrument as early as next summer.

Recent findings suggest that even when contact with Voyager 1 is eventually lost, the spacecraft will leave a lasting legacy—especially for any future such far-traveling missions, should NASA or another space agency launch one. A successor to Voyager might, for instance, have new devices such as a dust instrument to better analyze the interstellar medium or cameras to give astronomers a better view of these distant stretches of the cosmos, Rankin claims.

“I would hope that the Voyagers and their reaching interstellar space has taught us the lesson that we've got to just keep reaching for the stars,” she adds.

Industry observers note that every mission must meet its end, though. And Badaruddin’s best guess is that Voyager 1’s could come in the next three to five years, as the plutonium-238 powering it decays further. Once the craft transmits its final signal to Earth, it will still continue its silent tour of the galaxy.

But Badaruddin acknowledges he’s part of a lineage of mission managers who have said that the spacecraft only has a few years left, only to be proven wrong. “The Big Bang was a rabbit we pulled out of a hat. As long as we can keep finding rabbits, we can keep going,” he claims. “Don’t bet against Voyager.”.

Bayern Munich boss Vincent Kompany states he is "very healthy" and grateful for all of the support he has received as he prepares to return to the dugout on Friday.

The 40-year-old former Manchester City captain was taken to hospital after falling ill while watching the club's second team train last month.

Kompany was diagnosed with meningeal irritation - an inflammation of the protective membrane surrounding the brain and spinal cord.

Speaking at a news conference on Thursday he thanked the club, medical staff, players, coaches and fans for their support.

"It was very intense," he stated.

In a recent development, "At the time, it was a new experience. Looking back, everything went perfectly. I received support right away, from the club and the doctors. I'm very grateful.

According to recent reports, "You try to stay calm and wait until you have the results. It was a positive process, all the tests were positive.

In a recent development, "I have to say, I'm very healthy. We did a lot of tests, and they all came back fine. In those quiet moments, you also try to learn.

"Now I feel very good again and I'm happy to be back with the team.".

While he has been recovering Kompany's assistant Aaron Danks has led the side to four wins and a draw.

It has been revealed that "I'd also like to thank the coaching community," Kompany added. "We're always competing, but almost every coach has reached out to me, even if we've played against each other and perhaps argued as well. That's a beautiful thing.".

Bayern, for whom England captain Harry Kane has been in fine form, are top of the Bundesliga, level on points with Borussia Dortmund.

Elon Musk claims SpaceX’s Starship, already the largest rocket on Earth, will get even bigger with next-gen V4 model

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (862 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As usual, SpaceX and its founder Elon Musk are thinking big.
  • Industry observers note that the firm recovered the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever on Saturday (Nov.
  • According to recent reports, it was a huge moment for SpaceX, bringing its vision of full and rapid rocket reuse much closer to reality.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As usual, SpaceX and its founder Elon Musk are thinking big.

Industry observers note that the firm recovered the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever on Saturday (Nov. 14), plucking it out of the sky with the "chopstick" arms of its Texas launch tower.

According to recent reports, it was a huge moment for SpaceX, bringing its vision of full and rapid rocket reuse much closer to reality. But Elon Musk isn't one to dwell on the past or rest on laurels, so he soon outlined an even more ambitious future for Starship.

"Starship V4 will be ~70m [230 feet] long, which is roughly a 40% length increase and allows >60% more propellant load," Musk remarked via X, the social media platform he owns, on Sunday evening (Nov. 15). "Engine count will be raised to 9, with 3 more Raptor-Vacuum engines added, and these will be higher-thrust V4 engines.".

Industry observers note that the current version of Starship — the one that launched Friday (Nov. 13) on the vehicle's 15th test flight — is the V3. It's the largest and most powerful rocket ever built, standing 408 feet (124 m) tall when fully stacked with its Super Heavy first stage and Ship upper stage.

V3's Ship is 171 feet (52 m) tall and features six of SpaceX's Raptor V3 engines. (The similarly reusable Super Heavy V3 booster is powered by 33 Raptors.) So, as Musk noted in his post, the V4 Ship will be quite an upgrade in size and power.

Starship Die Cast Rocket Model Was $47.99 Now $39.99 on Amazon.

In a recent development, even if you can't see SpaceX's Starship in person, you can score a model of your own. Standing at 13.77 inches (35 cm), this is a 1:375 ratio of SpaceX's Starship as a desktop model. The materials here are alloy steel and it weighs just 225g.

To provide a little perspective about that vehicle's planned dimensions: The V4 Ship will be the same height as a fully stacked Falcon 9, SpaceX's workhorse two-stage rocket, and much broader: Ship is 30 feet (9 m) across, while the Falcon 9's payload fairing is 17.1 feet (5.2 m) wide.

According to recent reports, this isn't the first we've heard about a V4 Starship. Back in August 2025, for example, Musk posted a graphic showing Starship's planned progression from the V2 to the V3 to the V4, which he said is expected to debut in 2027.

Industry observers note that that slide pegs the future Starship's total height at 466 feet (142 m), 200 feet (61 m) of which would be Ship. But those numbers are out of date, Musk stressed in the post, saying that V4 is "probably closer to 150m height.".

So, yeah: If all goes according to proposal, the next Starship will be nearly 500 feet tall.

Starship V4 will be ~70m long, which is roughly a 40% length increase and allows >60% more propellant load. Engine count will be raised to 9, with 3 more Raptor-Vacuum engines added, and these will be higher thrust V4 engines.November 16, 2026.

The original Starship Flight 15 mission plan called for a double chopsticks catch, with both Super Heavy and Ship coming back to the launch tower for recovery.

Sources indicate that this would have been feasible, as the catches were scheduled a day apart: Super Heavy would land just 6.5 minutes after launch, while Ship would circle Earth for 22.5 hours, and deploy a batch of SpaceX's Starlink V3 internet satellites, before coming home. (Ship ended up delivering the satellites as planned.).

Recent findings suggest that the twofer didn't happen, however; Super Heavy experienced a low-fuel alarm and diverted to a Gulf of Mexico splashdown on Friday as a result. But that wasn't a huge deal, as SpaceX had already pulled off Super Heavy catches on three previous Starship flights.

The Ship catch was unprecedented, because it's been a taller order. Ship returns to Earth from orbit, so it comes in faster and hotter. SpaceX hadn't even tried the maneuver before Flight 15, so executing it was a very big deal.

According to recent reports, "That was the missing link," SpaceX's Dan Huot remarked during the manufacturer's Ship-landing webcast on Saturday. "We caught a Starship, and now everything changes.".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Fans from the UK can vote from the five-player shortlist of Jude Bellingham, Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe, Rodri and Lamine Yamal.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Voting is now open for the BBC Men's Footballer of the Year 2026 award, which will be presented at Sports Personality of the Year.

Fans from the UK can vote from the five-player shortlist of Jude Bellingham, Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe, Rodri and Lamine Yamal.

The vote closes on Friday, 27 November at 09:00 GMT.

The winner of the award - new for this year - will be presented during the live Sports Personality of the Year show on Sunday, 13 December.

Alex Kay-Jelski, Director of BBC Sport, noted: "From the drama and excitement of the men's World Cup to the moments that have captivated fans across the domestic and international game, 2026 has given us so much to celebrate.

"Our inaugural BBC Men's Footballer of the Year award is about recognising the players who have made this year so special, inspired fans and left their mark on the game.

"It's a fantastic shortlist, and I can't wait to see who the public choose as our first-ever winner.".

The shortlist was selected by an expert panel comprising former international players and some of the BBC's most respected football voices, bringing together a wealth of experience and insight from across the game.

The panel included Cesar Azpilicueta (Spain), Scott Brown (Scotland), Olivier Giroud (France), Shay Given (Republic of Ireland), Hassan Kachloul (Morocco), Lucas Leiva (Brazil), Benni McCarthy (South Africa), Alan Shearer, Ellen White (both England) and Ashley Williams (Wales).

Read more on the five contenders and cast your vote below.

In a recent development, sorry, this vote cannot be loaded. In order to vote you need to enable JavaScript in your browser.

Meet the SPOTY Men's Footballer of the Year contenders.

Club: Real Madrid Position: Midfield.

Bellingham made history this summer as he became the first Englishman to score as many as seven goals at a major tournament.

In a superb World Cup for the midfielder, he memorably netted twice in back-to-back games to help the Three Lions beat Mexico and Norway.

That meant he joined exalted tech giant as the first player to score two or more goals in successive World Cup knockout games since Diego Maradona in 1986, and the second youngest in history behind Pele in 1958.

Bellingham also became the youngest European player to make an appearance at four different major tournaments, and also reached the milestone of 50 caps at a younger age than any other England men's player.

The goals continued to flow for Real Madrid, too, with Bellingham notching his 50th for the club to move above the legendary Zinedine Zidane in the Los Blancos' all-time scoring charts.

Bellingham was recently joined in the England squad by his brother Jobe.

Club: Bayern Munich Position: Forward.

In a stunning year of goalscoring, Kane become the first Englishman for 25 years (and only fifth in history) to win the Ballon d'Or - awarded to the world's best footballer.

His tally of 73 goals in 65 matches for club and country during a stellar 2025-26 season has only been surpassed in one of Europe's top five leagues by Lionel Messi's 82 for Barcelona and Argentina in 2011-12.

Kane scored 61 of those goals in just 51 appearances for Bayern Munich as he helped the Bavarians to a league and cup double. His total was 19 more than any other player in Europe's top five divisions.

Already England's record goalscorer, he surpassed Peter Shilton's mark of 125 appearances to become the most-capped Englishman in history.

Six goals at this summer's World Cup also helped him overtake Gary Lineker as the Three Lions' record scorer at the tournament, while he joined David Beckham as the only Englishmen to score in three separate World Cups.

Kane scored his first England goal 79 seconds into his debut in 2015.

Club: Real Madrid Position: Forward.

Mbappe came out on top of an enthralling tussle with Lionel Messi at the 2026 World Cup to become the leading goalscorer in the tournament's history.

The France forward, who is still only 27, took his tally to 22 from just three World Cups to finish one ahead of the great Argentine.

Mbappe's 10 goals from eight games this summer meant he won his second World Cup Golden Boot - a feat no player has managed before.

It also made him the first man to reach double figures at a World Cup since Gerd Muller in 1970, with only Just Fontaine (13) and Sandor Kocsis (11) having scored more goals in a single tournament.

Other achievements in a standout year included him finishing runner-up in the Ballon d'Or awards and overtaking Olivier Giroud as France's all-time leading goalscorer.

He scored 25 times to retain his title as La Liga's top scorer during a 2025-26 campaign in which he netted 42 goals in all competitions for Real Madrid.

Mbappe has won eight consecutive league golden boots.

Club: Barcelona Position: Midfield.

Midfield maestro Rodri earned yet another accolade in his incredible career when he was awarded the Golden Ball trophy for the World Cup's best player.

By captaining Spain to glory in the US, Rodri became only the fourth male player to win the World Cup, European Championship, Champions League and Ballon d'Or - following in the footsteps of legendary Germans Gerd Muller and Franz Beckenbauer and France's Zinedine Zidane.

His achievements were made all the more special given doubts remained over whether he would recapture his best form after a long recovery from a serious knee injury in 2024.

Industry observers note that then Manchester City boss Pep Guardiola predicted he would return to his best at the World Cup and he was right. Rodri completed 756 passes there - the most in the tournament since records began in 1966.

His final season at Manchester City before departing for Barcelona ended in familiar fashion with a domestic cup double taking his trophy haul with the club to 14.

Rodri scored the goal that won Manchester City the Champions League in 2023.

Club: Barcelona Position: Forward.

Lamine Yamal continues to rewrite the record books with his astonishing exploits for club and country.

It has been revealed that just days after his 19th birthday, the Spaniard became the youngest footballer to have played in - and won - both a World Cup and a European Championship. The only players younger than him to play in a World Cup final are Brazil's Pele in 1958 and Giuseppe Bergomi for Italy in 1982.

For the second year running, his performances led to a podium place at the Ballon d'Or and at the same award ceremony he became the first footballer in history to win the Young Talent of the Year three years in succession.

It has been revealed that at club level, he was named La Liga's Best Player courtesy of a starring role in Barcelona's title success. The teenager ended the season with an impressive 24 goals and 18 assists across all competitions.

He recently broke Kylian Mbappe's record for the most goals by a teenager in Champions League history.

Lamine Yamal was 16 years and 362 days when he scored at the European Championship in 2024.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto VI is out in some parts of the world (Editor's note: Who's to say you don't live in New Zealand, too?). The early reviewers all say it's incredible, and according to Rockstar, there may be more to come.

Industry observers note that that piece of reporting comes courtesy of Kotaku, whose reviewer Zack Zwiezen noted that he had played more than 130 hours of the game without ever visiting certain parts of the enormous GTA 6 map. These areas include a zoo and two large casinos (where gambling is apparently not allowed), and are never mentioned in the main story or any side missions.

According to Rockstar Games VP of design Stephen Donkin, the in-game map was built for more than just this initial launch period.

"The map has been built for the long term and with many factors in mind,” Donkin told Kotaku. "So there are a few areas on the map that give us options in the future should we have a gameplay or narrative need for them.".

Donkin's response seems to indicate that there will be more content coming to GTA 6 in the future, which is not surprising in and of itself. It's only mildly surprising that Rockstar would openly acknowledge that fact on launch day (in Fresh Zealand, anyway). Where this gets interesting is that Donkin could be referring to a couple of different things, namely new single-player missions or a still-unannounced online mode.

It has been revealed that GTA V rather infamously never got single-player DLC, despite Rockstar promising such a thing shortly after its launch in 2013. Instead, GTA Online became massively successful, and that took priority. GTA 6 could be an opportunity to right that wrong, or it could be a repeat of history.

In September, Games Informer published interviews with Rockstar leaders that revealed just how gargantuan the map really is.

Sources indicate that rockstar confirmed it's the largest map it's ever made, and roughly twice as major as the GTA 5 map and three times as big as the Red Dead Redemption 2 map. But it's not just about size. Rockstar said it's also much denser and includes more interior spaces gamers can explore.

The map presently has six main regions: Vice City, Leonida Keyes, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia, and Mount Kalaga National Park, all inspired by different parts of Florida.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Florence Pugh isn’t worrying about the rumor mill, darling.

The East of Eden star responded to speculation that she’s had work done after fans theorized the reason for her newly chiseled jawline.

After a content creator noted she thinks “that we can all collectively agree that Hollywood seems to have this thing against softer features,” with stars wanting “this sculpted, snatched look,” in a video shared to Evie Magazine’s Instagram Nov. 17, Pugh addressed why “her jaw is more sharp.”.

As the Marvel star stated of the side-by-side photos of herself in the video, “Guys. I turned 30. I’m a woman. [Bodies] and faces change.”.

Sources indicate that “It’s not that deep, the fact that people can’t even tell between what’s aging and what’s surgery is disturbing,” she added in the post’s comments section. “Sadly puppy fluff doesn’t last forever.”.

She further addressed her shock over the matter in a vulnerable social media statement.

Recent findings suggest that “I find it so stressful waking up and have thousands of people talking about you and your body in ways that you can’t even comprehend,” she wrote on Instagram Nov. 18. “I woke up the other morning and quite a lot of you were discussing my face and body in such a disturbing way.”.

She noted, "I learnt online that I had been on ozempic? I learnt that I’d had upper bleph? Lower bleph? Filler? Face lipo? Bucal fat remover? Chin surgery? Nose surgery?!”.

“I have spent my whole career defending and protecting bodies that just grow the way they grow,” she added. “I was subjected to fat shaming in the business from the moment I started and I have loved everytime I get to tell someone to f--k off when they are being inappropriate about my weight, and I’m not changing that now just because you’ve all said so.”.

And just for the record, the Little Women actress wants fans to know she’s perfectly happy in the skin she’s in.

According to recent reports, “I have never been on Ozempic,” she wrote. “I have NEVER done any face surgery. And don’t EVER say that I didn’t make my own nose, I’ve always had that beautiful ski slope. Even as a baby!”.

Rather, Pugh credits any difference in her appearance to a lifestyle change.

“Here’s the truth, I turned 30 and my Latest Year’s resolution was to change my relationship with alcohol, and to be able to do at least one pull up in the gym,” she continued. “For the first time in my ENTIRE career, I have had the opportunity to be rested, to sleep, to wake up and work out and to eat regularly and healthily.”.

And she won’t let internet fodder about her body throw her off her game.

According to recent reports, “I’ve f--king worked so hard to clean my head and clean my body because I don’t want to allow space for negativity in my mind to grow,” she added. “I’m looking after myself, and that’s literally it.”.

Keep reading for more stars who have set the record straight on getting cosmetic enhancements….

The Euphoria actress confirmed in December 2025 that she hasn't had a boob job.

As costar Amanda Seyfried told her during Vanity Fair's Lie Detector Test, “There’s been a question on everybody’s minds recently, and I just have to ask, are your boobs real?”.

“Yes,” Sydney responded. “I’ve never gotten any work done anywhere.”.

She shared in December 2025 that she's never gotten filler.

Industry observers note that “As you are going along in your journey, I don’t think that you should overdo it with surgery, filler, Botox,” she told People. “You don’t need to do too much. Take it easy. Less is always better.".

Travis Barker and ex Shanna Moakler's daughter has been open about her use of lip fillers but denies having cosmetic surgery.

In February 2024, she shared photos of herself wearing a bikini on Instagram, to which a user commented, "This child has done alot of cosmetic surgery @ a very young age, I hope she doesn't over do it! She looks good now!".

Sources indicate that the rapper responded, "I really appreciate the love! I'm natural, besides my lips, accept the fact I'm naturally beautiful.".

Recent findings suggest that the Twilight alum told Harper's Bazaar U.K. in 2015 she will "never" get plastic surgery, adding, "I am so freaked out by the idea of doing anything. And maybe that's completely arrogant but I don't want to change anything about myself. I think the women who do are losing their minds. It's vandalism.".

It has been revealed that the Devil Wears Prada star told Good Housekeeping in 2008. "You have to embrace getting older. Life is precious, and when you've lost a lot of people, you realize each day is a gift.".

The "God's Proposal" rapper shut down rumors in September 2025 that he had plastic surgery to make his abs more defined, explaining the fan speculation was a result of using a photo editing app.

"I came from the gym, I was sweaty in that pic," he noted during an episode of Bobbi Althoff’s Not This Again podcast. "Maybe I heightened the saturation or something on it.".

Sources indicate that he added, "I think I hit it too hard. They don't look like that.".

While Drake noted that people go under the knife "all the time," he isn’t one of them.

It has been revealed that "People also say that I got a BBL," he continued, referencing the popular Brazilian Butt Lift procedure. "They call me 'BBL Drizzy.'".

The supermodel opened up about why she's all about embracing her skin at every age.

"This is a 58 year old face without fillers, Botox or surgery in good light with professional gorgeous makeup," she wrote in an August 2023 Instagram caption. "I have chosen not to put anything 'into' my face.".

She continued, "Some days, I like it. I feel like my face has gained character even as it's lost its youthful prettiness. And it seems a fair trade off.".

The Oscar winner revealed whether or not she's gotten plastic surgery.

"My face is changing," she told Allure in an interview published August 2023, "and I love that my face is changing and aging. People think I had a facelift. They're like, 'What did she do to her face?' I'm like, 'Bitch, I'm just aging! It doesn't mean I got bad plastic surgery. This is just what happens.'".

Sources indicate that the Pitch Perfect alum admitted she's never gotten any cosmetic injectables, telling People in 2023, "I've never put a needle in my face. And by the way, most people do it and truly, there's no judgement. But I make my living with my face.".

She added, "Basically I'm terrified of f--king it up.".

The Magic Mike actress set the record straight on whether or not she's gotten facial injectables. "No Botox!" she put it bluntly on Kelly Ripa's Let's Talk Off Camera podcast.

The "Summertime Sadness" singer denied having a surgical procedure on her nose after a fan referenced her "natural nose.".

“Still never even been under the knife or anesthesia in my life for the 15th year in a row!!” Lana wrote on Instagram in September 2025, per a screenshot captured by People. “But if u use filler like [my doctor] used to- to build up the bridge of your nose it looks tall no bump. Takes seven minutes.”.

According to recent reports, the nonsurgical rhinoplasty Lana referred is “a cosmetic procedure where dermal fillers are used to temporarily change the shape of your nose,” according to the Cleveland Clinic. Though the procedure is less invasive, the results only last up to six months.

In 2021, the supermodel, who rose to fame in the '90s as one of the first, sued Zeltiq Aesthetics, alleging that its CoolScupting fat-reducing procedures that she underwent in 2015 and 2016 left her "permanently disfigured." The parties reached a settlement in the case in 2022.

Sources indicate that jenny from the Block continues to look like Jenny from the Block. In January 2021, she told an Instagram user, "I have never done Botox or any other injectables or surgery!! Just sayin'.".

The Friends actress did have a nose job when she was younger to fix a deviated septum, but has spoke out against Botox and other facial fillers.

"There is also this pressure in Hollywood to be ageless," she told Yahoo! Beauty in 2014. "I think what I have been witness to, is seeing women trying to stay ageless with what they are doing to themselves. I am grateful to learn from their mistakes, because I am not injecting s--t into my face.".

"I've probably tried everything. I would be scared to go under the knife, but you know, talk to me when I'm 50. I'll try anything. Except I won't do Botox again, because I looked crazy," the actress told Harper's Bazaar in 2013.

Sources indicate that the Charlie's Angels alum told InStyle magazine in 2012, "I say, don't fight the rings on the trunk of a tree. Just keep counting 'em.".

"The idea of not looking like myself scares me," she added.

The Love Actually actress told The Telegraph in 2011, "I'm not fiddling about with myself. We're in this awful youth-driven thing now where everybody needs to look 30 at 60.".

Industry observers note that "Nah. It's not my thing," the Oscar winner told MORE magazine in 2007. "I don't have anything against it for other people. Whatever they want to do, I'm fine with it. For me, it's really a self-image thing. Like, I'd rather have somebody go, "Wow, that girl has a major nose" than 'Wow, that girl has a bad nose job.' I'd rather have a comment about who I am than about something that identifies me as being ashamed of who I am.".

In 2011, the pop star told Harper's Bazaar, "I think that promoting insecurity in the form of plastic surgery is infinitely more harmful than an artistic expression related to body modification.".

In a recent development, in 2011, the Titanic star told the U.K. newspaper The Telegraph that cosmetic surgery goes against her morals, the way her parents brought her up and what she considers to be "natural beauty.".

According to recent reports, "I will never give in," she added. "I am an actress, I don't want to freeze the expression of my face.".

China Renaissance, a top dealmaker in the country’s tech industry, noted it would suspend trading of its shares and delay the release of its annual results because it still can’t get in touch with its founder.

Industry observers note that bao Fan, 52, started the boutique investment bank in 2005 and has been unreachable since the middle of February, according to the manufacturer. Shares in China Renaissance have plunged since Bao went missing, at one point dropping as much as 50%.

It has been revealed that china Renaissance stated in late February that it had learned Bao was “cooperating in an investigation” being carried out by certain authorities in the country. It gave no other details.

Chinese media have reported Bao might be assisting in an investigation related to a former executive at China Renaissance.

It has been revealed that in a filing on Sunday, China Renaissance remarked auditors couldn’t complete their work or sign off on their report because of Bao’s absence. The board was also unable to give an estimate about when it would be able to approve its audited results for 2022 or dispatch its annual report by an April 30 deadline as required by Hong Kong’s listing rules.

Missing Chinese billionaire CEO assisting authorities in investigation, company claims.

Trading in the firm’s shares was suspended from Monday as a result.

Bao is known as a veteran dealmaker who works closely with top technology companies in China. He helped broker the 2015 merger between two of the country’s leading food delivery services, Meituan and Dianping. Today, the combined manufacturer’s “super app” platform is ubiquitous in China.

His team has also invested in US-listed Chinese electric vehicle makers Nio (NIO) and Li Auto and helped Chinese internet giants Baidu (BIDU) and JD.com (JD) complete their secondary listings in Hong Kong.

Over the weekend, China’s top anti-graft watchdog debuted an investigation into Liu Liange, former party secretary and chairman of Bank of China, according to a statement by the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection and the State Supervision Commission. The bank is state-owned and one of the country’s four biggest lenders.

In a recent development, liu is suspected of “serious violations of discipline and law,” the statement noted. He is among the most senior financial executives targeted in a broader financial crackdown by President Xi Jinping.

In January, Wang Bin, former party chief and chairman of China Life Insurance, was charged by national-level prosecutors with taking bribes and hiding overseas savings.

— Michelle Toh contributed reporting.

Industry News: German economy returns to growth, so why is the country still worried?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that is Germany's economy back on the up?
  • At the 2026 Mechanical Engineering Summit in Berlin this week, the mood was sullen.
  • Sources indicate that the mechanical and plant engineering sector was the backbone of German industry for decades.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that is Germany's economy back on the up? The answer to that question depends on your perspective.

At the 2026 Mechanical Engineering Summit in Berlin this week, the mood was sullen. "A year ago, I said here: We are angry. Today I must say: We are stunned," Bertram Kawlath, president of the Mechanical Engineering Industry Association (VDMA), said in his opening remarks on Tuesday.

Sources indicate that the mechanical and plant engineering sector was the backbone of German industry for decades. It once employed more than a million people; now 15,000 positions are being cut every month. Production has shrunk about 20% since 2018.

Kawlath criticized the federal government's infighting and lack of reform, as well as what the companies consider a continued high bureaucracy and tax burden.

"[We are] stunned by the whitewashing in so many government statements. Stunned by the increasingly visible decline of our country as a business location.".

In a recent development, german Chancellor Friedrich Merz promised quick reforms and a rapidly noticeable economic upswing when he took office in May 2025. A year and a half later, reality has caught up with him.

Merz's coalition of his conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU), its Bavarian sister party the Christian Social Union, (CSU), along with the center-left Social Democrats(SPD), keeps running into trouble. In addition, there are crises and wars. The German economy is facing more headwinds than seldom before, Merz said in October at the German Employers' Day conference in Berlin.

Given the circumstances, small successes are even more meaningful. "A heartfelt thanks for the good news you bring," Merz remarked when he received the autumn report of the Council of Economic Experts in Berlin, which predicted economic growth of 1.3% for 2026 and 1% for 2027.

The economic experts have a German government mandate to independently analyze business activity and make recommendations for economic policy. Earlier this year, they were much more pessimistic.

It has been revealed that "The German economy has recovered quicker than expected from the energy price shock sparked by the war in Iran," noted Monika Schnitzer, chair of the expert advisory board, explaining the prognosis. "We see a significant economic recovery, driven by surprisingly strong exports and high government spending.".

It has been revealed that the chancellor, who celebrated his 71st birthday on November 11, spoke of "encouraging signals" in his address. "The economy in Germany is slowly on the rise again. Considering the many crises in Germany, it was not totally expected that we would manage that.".

Industry observers note that but these improved prospects do not change the long-term problems. An ageing society means the bills for pensions, health and caregiving are constantly rising.

It has been revealed that at the same time, the number of working-age people who finance these services is sinking. That puts increasing pressure on the public purse. According to Berlin's financial planning, social welfare costs, defense and interest on debt will account for 80% of the spending in the federal government's budget.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

According to recent reports, "We must realize that in the long term the expected revenues in the federal budget will not be enough to cover the planned expenses," Schnitzer warned. The growth rates are far below what is needed to secure the same level of prosperity as previous decades in the long term.

"To grow out of this budgetary predicament, we would need levels of economic growth which we haven't experienced in Germany for the past 50 years," she said.

Recent findings suggest that the government is at the moment in final deliberations over its 2027 budget; spending upwards of €555 billion ($615 billion) is planned. Because revenue won't be enough to cover it, the government is planning to take on more than €118 billion in fresh debt. Adding the debt-financed special funds for infrastructure and the military, the new borrowing adds up to almost €204 billion.

It has been revealed that the economic experts have warned that if Germany continues with this path, the debt-to-GDP ratio could rise to 100% by 2040. This ratio indicates how high the national debt is in relation to annual economic output. At the end of 2025, it was 63.5%.

It has been revealed that germany is the only country of the world's leading democratic industrialized nations (G7) to still hold a AAA rating, the best possible credit rating in finance markets. It signals to investors the smallest possible default risk for German government bonds. "I want it to stay that way," Merz emphasized.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

According to recent reports, however, taking on less debt will not be simple. "A reduction in debt-based financing presents policymakers with a consolidation task of historic proportions and will require tough decisions," mentioned Schnitzer. The belt-tightening must, however, be designed to enable growth. Some recommendations include reducing environmentally harmful tax benefits — like the energy tax breaks for diesel fuel.

The so-called "mothers' pension", a pension subsidy for older parents, should be revoked, mentioned the experts. Tax increases could become necessary in the medium term, for example with value-added tax.

"The burden should be shared fairly between generations and societal groups," Schnitzer noted.

In a recent development, according to the chancellor, the experts' message has been received. Solid state finances are an matter in Germany but also throughout the European Union. Merz noted there needs to be a consolidation course, adding that politicians have a duty to the younger generation. Reforms are needed, especially when it comes to social security systems.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Sources indicate that economic researchers are setting their hopes on increasing companies' productivity. Put simply, productivity describes how much a company can generate with its employees, machinery and resources in a set time.

According to the Council of Economic Experts, there is enormous variation even within the same industries. In Germany, the top companies are up to five times as productive as the weakest enterprises.

If the less productive companies caught up, economic growth could increase significantly, it said in the report. "Upcoming technologies and business models could drive peak productivity and allow new highly productive companies to develop.".

But innovations need capital. It's here that the Ifo Economic Research Institute sees considerable deficiencies.

In a recent development, new evaluations show that German universities produce significantly fewer successful business startups than their counterparts in the United Kingdom or United States. For example, for every 1,000 students, about 14 venture capital-backed founders emerge from the vicinity of Stanford University each year. In Cambridge, the European leader, it's 3.5. In Munich, by contrast, it's only 0.5.

There continues to be an abundance of inventors and tinkerers in Germany, especially in mechanical engineering. However, the message from the industry summit in Berlin was that for renewed success, labor costs must come down. Suggestions included longer working hours and more flexibility for employers around job protection.

According to recent reports, the intention was not to cut employees' wages and salaries. However, a new study by the German Economic Institute commissioned for the German Mechanical Engineering Industry Association showed that extending the working week by an hour alone would increase real gross domestic product by 1.5% in the coming five years.

This article was originally written in German.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Spain Under-21 striker admits the pace of the Premier League has surprised him but indicates he must stay calm over goal drought at Fulham.
  • It has been revealed that the first thing Rita Hayworth’s great nephew claims when he walks in is: “Sorry I’m late.” Gonzalo García is not late, but it’s very like him: he is impeccably polite, accommodating, and there’s an almost gentle quality to him, a calm that’s not common but can help, especially in moments when the pressure builds.
  • Time to talk, so let’s start with tinseltown, the family tale.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Spain Under-21 striker admits the pace of the Premier League has surprised him but indicates he must stay calm over goal drought at Fulham.

It has been revealed that the first thing Rita Hayworth’s great nephew claims when he walks in is: “Sorry I’m late.” Gonzalo García is not late, but it’s very like him: he is impeccably polite, accommodating, and there’s an almost gentle quality to him, a calm that’s not common but can help, especially in moments when the pressure builds. There’s a reason one of the coaches standing in the rain by the pitch where Spain’s under-21s have just finished training says everyone here loves García. The Fulham striker shakes hands, introduces himself and ducks into the dressing room to change; then a few minutes later he’s back, apologising for a wait that wasn’t one.

Time to talk, so let’s start with tinseltown, the family tale. García laughs. His great-aunt, born Margarita Carmen Cansino, was among the biggest stars in Hollywood, although he’s not sure he’s seen any of her films. His grandfather was a surgeon and others in the family followed. His uncles played rugby for Spain, but that wasn’t his thing. As for him, he enrolled in a degree in business management and analytics, and reckons he might have liked law, yet even that wasn’t his chosen field.

Hayworth’s family was from Seville province. “I know she was a great actress but I’m afraid I have to admit I’m not one for old films,” García concedes in an even tone. “My uncles played rugby for Ciencias and practically all of them were in the national team together. They tried to get me to play with my cousins, but I was always more into football.” He was good at it too: another Spain international, the Club World Cup’s top scorer, playing for Real Madrid.

Sources indicate that then this summer, with opportunities limited, he joined Fulham, his introductory interview conducted in impeccable English. Having joined Madrid aged 10, he was leaving home for the first time, as Fulham’s record signing, at 22. He had the language and intelligence to embrace it. As for being uprooted, he was used to that, growing up in Argentina and Chile as well as Spain.

It has been revealed that “From very little my parents impressed upon me the importance of study, learning languages,” García indicates. “I’m at Villanueva university [in Madrid]. I started with dual honours business and analytics although that became difficult with my profession. Now it’s just business, and I’m trying to arrange with the university how best to handle it [from London]. My parents considered it fundamental to speak English and I was always at international schools.

“Every two or three years we would change city. Obviously, there would be phases when I felt: ‘Pfff, again?!’ Having to move home because of my parents’ work. But I look back and feel grateful because, seen with perspective, it gives you opportunities to meet latest people, see new places, learn. I’ve always had foreign friends with whom I spoke English.”.

According to recent reports, garcía has been joined at Fulham by César Palacios and Manuel Ángel from Madrid’s academy. Three 22-year-olds, like your very own Erasmus course. “Nah,” García states, laughing. “I wouldn’t call it an Erasmus because we’re talking about a massive, ambitious career step. We’re grateful for the trust placed in us. I’ve been pleasantly surprised by London, a huge city with people from all nationalities and cultures and Fulham fit the situation I was in, the desire to grow.

It has been revealed that “Álvaro Arbeloa explained the project, convinced me. I’d worked with him in Madrid. He knows me perfectly, how far he can push me. Equally, I know what he wants of me. That helps … [Arbeloa] told me it was a project that it will take time but that he needed me. I’m very, very happy. It’s one of the world’s best leagues, if not the best.”.

It has been revealed that and the toughest? Is English football as wild as it looks? “Yes!” García replies. “They had told me it was demanding, hard, but …” He cracks up. “I have to admit it still surprised me. That first game against Chelsea, I finished really, really tired. It was box to box, intense, a lot of running. Bit by bit I’m adapting. The intensity and pace is very different.

It has been revealed that “Spain is more tactical, a bit more technical. English football is pace. You can’t lose concentration for a second, not a second. Anything can happen any moment. How many Premier League games are decided late? Suddenly there’s a goal in the 90th minute and again on 93. It’s your corner and their chance. The level of concentration, that constant transition, is what most sets the Premier League apart.”.

Despite defeat on that opening day against Chelsea, García scored. A superb goal followed against AFC Wimbledon in the Carabao Cup. “It was super special to do it at Craven Cottage – I love how close the fans are; they can reach out and touch you. But I don’t consider myself someone who’s easily satisfied. I’m not like that. I always want more, more, more.”.

García hasn’t scored since and Fulham went five league games without a win, pressure building. Which is where the calmness comes in. By the time they faced Hull, Arbeloa appeared on the edge of the sack, questions asked about his signings, García especially. Were three Madrid academy kids really what Fulham needed? Was the coach’s relationship with them not such a good thing after all?

Recent findings suggest that no player is impermeable to what is stated, García admits, but he insists: “We treat that as outside noise. And we all knew that the beginning wouldn’t be easy. There’s a change of cycle: the coach goes, a new coach comes, there are signings, a different system, idea. Everyone has to adapt: those already at the club and those of us who are new. We’re young too. Results weren’t going our way but we had good intentions: to play good football, build, apply the manager’s ideas bit by bit. We had to remain calm.”.

Fulham go into Saturday’s game at Manchester City unbeaten in four in the league, the sense of them shifting towards something more pragmatic not shared by García. “I don’t think we changed anything against Hull,” he says of a game Fulham won 1-0. “We didn’t do anything we weren’t already doing. Nothing. Maybe we controlled the small details that hurt us but the idea was the same. The players were very clear what the manager asked, very firm: it was just a question of time. You have to be patient. If you watch Fulham, you see the manager’s idea: have the ball, construct attacks well, show maximum intensity constantly with and without the ball. Aggressive, ambitious.”.

It has been revealed that chances are coming for García but goals aren’t. He has started every league game but not scored or assisted since the opening day. Yet if there is a sense of a man feeling the pressure, that’s not repeated here; instead there’s an evenness, an ease. And a smile when another, more welcome, stat is raised: he has made more off-the-ball runs into the area than anyone. Something to hold on to, perhaps, a process that will pay off. “Really?” he says. “Well, I’m happy for people to see that a striker can help the team without the ball. In the end, it’s about following the manager’s instructions.”.

In the end though, teams will be judged on results and strikers on goals, price too. He knows: this is what he does, the path he chose. “Pressure depends on how you look at it, really,” García says. “Football is [very psychological]. It happens fast: it doesn’t give you time to enjoy good moments or linger on bad ones. It’s a rollercoaster: up there, down here. It’s not flat, but you maintain balance, work daily, improve: go in, focus, repeat.

“It’s not that I don’t ‘care’ about the price, it’s that the market is the market; it doesn’t depend on me. Calmness always, perspective … I know strikers are measured by goals but, well, the days I don’t score I’m completely sure I will be able to walk off the pitch and say that, no matter what happened, I helped my team, doing a load of other things. It is what it is.”.

It is also time. A head peers around the door, the bus is going. García holds out a hand, apologises again. “It’s been a pleasure,” he states.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • STARBASE, Texas — SpaceX has officially wrapped up the 15th test flight of its massive Starship rocket, successfully catching the vehicle's upper stage for the first time.
  • Flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX's Starbase facility here in South Texas on Friday (Nov.
  • It was the first-ever Ship catch, and a huge milestone toward SpaceX's ultimate goal: making Starship completely reusable.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

STARBASE, Texas — SpaceX has officially wrapped up the 15th test flight of its massive Starship rocket, successfully catching the vehicle's upper stage for the first time.

Flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX's Starbase facility here in South Texas on Friday (Nov. 13). The mission was billed as the first to bring both of Starship's stages, the Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage, back to the launch site for recovery. And, while SpaceX was forced to divert Super Heavy's return to an off-shore splashdown (and explosion), the upper stage managed to survive its 22-hour jaunt in orbit and plunge through the atmosphere for a picture-perfect catch by the launch tower back at Starbase.

It was the first-ever Ship catch, and a huge milestone toward SpaceX's ultimate goal: making Starship completely reusable.

In a recent development, liftoff occurred from Pad 2 at 5:47 p.m. EST (2247 GMT; 4:47 p.m. local time) on Friday, against a near cloudless blue sky. Super Heavy is powered by 33 Raptor 3 engines, which provide more than 18 million pounds of thrust at liftoff. And lift off the booster did.

Starship roared off the pad under the power of those Raptors, pulsing visible shockwaves through the plume ejected from the rocket's flame trench.

The first couple minutes of flight went nominally; the vehicle climbed into the sky, gearing up for the hot-staging separation of Super Heavy and Ship — all of which was visible for miles, thanks to the clear Texas skies.

Space.com's images taken from the media’s launch viewing area were shot on a Canon R5 Mark II, with an RF 200-800mm lens that made the sharp pictures of Starship’s liftoff and return possible from almost 4 miles away.

This mirrorless Canon has specs that make it one of the best cameras available right now, with impressive features and functionality, including a 45MP sensor and excellent high-ISO handling.

Check our in-depth Canon R5 Mark II review.

Recent findings suggest that A successful separation occurred at T+2:21 minutes, as Starship soared approximately 40 miles (65 km) overhead. Once disconnected from its booster, Ship increased its thrust and continued onward to space, while Super Heavy, reoriented for its boostback burn and return to Starbase.

According to recent reports, that return, however, did not go entirely as planned. Super Heavy experienced a low-fuel alarm and autonomously shifted to an offshore splashdown rather than a catch attempt at Starbase.

Super heavy performed its landing burn above the Gulf of Mexico before cutting its engines for a brief moment and exploding in a giant fireball.

This was an intentional detonation, courtesy of the vehicle's flight termination system.

According to recent reports, ship continued on to low Earth orbit, where it deployed a payload of 26 upgraded Starlink Version 3 satellites. It was the second batch of V3 Starlinks delivered during Starship’s recent flight tests, each of which has added what SpaceX says is the equivalent of 10 Falcon 9 Starlink V2 satellite rolls out worth of data capacity to its orbital constellation.

Recent findings suggest that flight 15 was also Starship's second-ever mission to orbit, and its longest so far. Ship spent nearly a full day in orbit, circling Earth a total of 14 times. During its jaunt in space, the spacecraft cleared three separate check points, which allowed SpaceX the opportunity to divert the vehicle for an ocean splashdown if needed, and finally was given the green light to attempt the first-ever Ship tower catch.

Recent findings suggest that at approximately 4:18 p.m. EST (2018 GMT, 3:18 p.m. local time in Texas) on Saturday (Nov. 14), the spacecraft broke through the cloud cover that blanketed the skies above Starbase as onlookers watched its bellyflop plunge toward the ground. Moments after becoming visible, Ship ignited its engines for a flip and burn maneuver, which oriented it upright and swung its trajectory into the tightening grip of the chopstick arms of Starbase's "Mechazilla" launch tower.

After a slight sway back and forth suspended above Earth in Mechazilla's embrace, Ship came to a complete rest, hanging motionless as a historic milestone in SpaceX’s pursuit of fully reusable spaceflight.

It hung there overnight as engineers, and even SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, inspected the spacecraft. Ship was lowered on Sunday (Nov. 15) and transported back to SpaceX's Starbase hanger bay for further checkouts.

SpaceX has not yet remarked whether Ship 42 will fly again, but its return gives engineers a chance to examine how the spacecraft held up through launch, nearly a day in orbit and atmospheric reentry.

Those findings will help inform upcoming flights as SpaceX ramps up production to continue testing Starship's capabilities.

Josh Dinner is Space.com's Spaceflight Staff Writer and a photographer with a passion for science and exploration. He has worked the space beat since 2016, covering the evolution of NASA's commercial spaceflight partnerships and crewed missions, planetary science missions, the Artemis program and humanity's return to the moon. He also enjoys building 1:144-scale model rockets and spacecraft. Find some of Josh's launch photography on Instagram, and follow him on X, where he mostly posts in haiku.

Drew Barrymore is always thinking about her little ones.

The Blended star admitted that her past as a party girl weighed especially heavy on her after welcoming daughters Olive, 14, and Frankie, 12, with ex-husband Will Kopelman.

“One of the many things I wanted to discuss with you was how much of my life I have spent in shame because of being a party culture person,” Barrymore told guest Jordan Firstman on the Nov. 17 episode of The Drew Barrymore Show. “And I don’t know why, but there’s a villainization of people who want to let loose, who want to imbibe, who want to dance, who want to let go and just get away from this very, very complex world sometimes.”.

She felt that judgement even more when journalists would ask “all the time” whether she would have children.

“And I know what they were saying is, ‘You are not capable, and if you even dared to have children, will they be able to live with the history that is so public?’” she explained. “And when I became a parent, that haunted me so badly, the judgment and ‘the partiers are bad people,’ and I don’t think that’s true.”.

Though the Charlie’s Angels alum has been candid about the mistakes she’s made in her youth, she’s also no stranger to keeping it real about motherhood.

It has been revealed that “All those parents who have it all together, and they’ve got hygiene and nutrition and schedules and boundaries, God bless you,” she said during a 2022 appearance on Chicks in the Office. “I didn’t know any of that stuff when I had my kids.”.

In a recent development, “I did not have the blueprint and I felt like a failure a lot,” she admitted. “I felt really overwhelmed and like, ‘I don’t know what I’m doing.’”.

But learning “on the job” only made her experience with motherhood sweeter. Plus, it gave her a nudge towards the person she always hoped to be.

Recent findings suggest that "I just love having a family," she told E! News in 2015. "I love my kids—I feel so blessed. I feel like I've never been better as a person [than I am] through my family.”.

"I feel like I was born the day my kids were,” she added, "and everything in life was like an experiment to learn to apply to them.".

#36097. Breaking: AI in classrooms: Fighting the great 'dumbing down'

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1411 w)

Breaking: AI in classrooms: Fighting the great 'dumbing down'

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1411 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Jakob is 15 years old and attends a secondary school for more academic students, known in Germany as a gymnasium.
  • Recent findings suggest that "I had a French test today, and yesterday I had ChatGPT explain a lot of the topics to me again," the student told DW.
  • Math, German, English, chemistry and even physics: In one click, the solution or the path to a solution is available thanks to AI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jakob is 15 years old and attends a secondary school for more academic students, known in Germany as a gymnasium. He and his classmates have already been using artificial intelligence-enabled tools, or AI, for the last two and a half years.

Recent findings suggest that "I had a French test today, and yesterday I had ChatGPT explain a lot of the topics to me again," the student told DW. Jakob isn't his real name, because he doesn't want to publicly admit he and many others of his age use AI to do their homework.

Math, German, English, chemistry and even physics: In one click, the solution or the path to a solution is available thanks to AI.

In science, this is called "cognitive outsourcing." Basically, the required thinking is shifted to another device, whether that's a calculator, notepad or a large language model (LLM) like ChatGPT.

There's a difference with AI, though. A notepad or calculator can take over a step or two but rarely the whole thought process. That's not the same for an LLM, which can handle the entire problem-solving process.

Jakob admitted he's also had an AI help him with his homework. "But only when I was really stuck," he insisted. And he's also aware that it can become a problem when AI does all your homework. "The students who get good grades tend not to do that," he explained.

Sources indicate that franziska Müller has been a German teacher for several decades and is currently teaching senior classes at a gymnasium. Her name has also been changed for privacy reasons.

"They can't even think for themselves anymore," she told DW, complaining about some of her classes.

Even in ordinary classes, some of the students type their questions into their tablets or phones, asking for AI assistance. And should they be called upon in class, she knows that they're reading out the answers that the AI has prepared for them and hoping nobody notices.

Müller believes students these days are less able to comprehend text. "Because they read less and let AI summarize almost everything for them," she said.

Several studies have reached very similar conclusions.

That includes the latest PISA (Program for International Student Assessment) study from September. PISA, which is run by the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development, regularly evaluates the abilities of 15-year-old students around the world.

It has been revealed that "Students who report using AI chatbots get lower scores in science, on average, than those who don't use AI," Andreas Schleicher, the OECD director for education and skills, wrote in his report in October. "This includes using AI to summarize texts they had to read, conduct preliminary research on a new topic, or draft texts for writing assignments.".

According to recent reports, with participants from more than 90 countries, PISA is considered the largest international comparative study of 15-year-olds worldwide. This year, German 15-year-olds posted their lowest PISA scores in the 25-year history of the study.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

"The connections are complex and depend heavily on how generative AI is used, but the central insight is simple: Just as we don't get fit by watching sports but by doing sports ourselves, learning doesn't come from consuming content, but from the mind's productive cognitive engagement with new material," Schleicher explained.

Put simply, those who don't exercise their brains risk becoming less intelligent.

US think tank, the Brookings Institution, has already argued that the risks of using AI in education outweigh the benefits.

Its own research, which included young participants from around the world, speaks of students losing "fundamental cognitive and durable skills as they increasingly rely on AI to perform learning's intellectual work," as well as the decline of critical thinking, memory, perseverance and independent judgment.

But what can be done against the power of ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, Gemini and Meta AI?

Newly introduced York Mayor Zohran Mamdani has banned the use of AI in public schools up to the eighth grade for the 2026 and 2027 school years — so that's up to about the age of 14 or 15.

Recent findings suggest that not everyone agrees this is the right thing to do. Julian Hinn, who teaches German to students aged between 15 and 18 in Germany, stated class members can still use AI apps on their mobile phones. "And anyone who thinks they won't use it at home is ignoring reality," Hinn told DW.

Germany's annual JIM study, which tracks teenagers' media use and device ownership, supports that view.

Ninety-one percent of young people surveyed in Germany, between the ages of 12 and 19, stated that they use at least one AI application. The study also reports that 74% use AI for homework and learning.

Recent findings suggest that the last JIM study actually dates back to 2024 so those percentages might be even higher now. Data on AI use in Asia, Latin America and the US from the Brookings study show similarly high figures.

It has been revealed that german politicians have recognized the problem. Although education in Germany is the responsibility of the individual federal states, the so-called Standing Conference of the Ministers of Education and Cultural Affairs, or KMK, has been issuing statements on the use of AI since 2024.

The KMK's statements have been rather vague though, saying only that students should be enabled to engage with AI in a critical, reflective and responsible manner.

Teachers and students alike are aware that AI can be a powerful support in the classroom.

"The AIs simply explain things much better than textbooks," said Jakob, adding that he'll often get an AI to explain basic concepts to him.

Industry observers note that sometimes teachers can't respond like an AI, Hinn conceded. "The AI ​​can respond much better to the language and needs of the students.".

In a recent development, that's why he thinks it's key to include AI in classes, starting from the 10th grade when students are around 15 or 16. Hinn doesn't think it should be introduced before that, when children's basic skills are still being developed.

In more senior classes, Hinn will encourage his students to question the AI critically. "We look at the quality of the solutions," he explained.

German teacher Müller has also integrated some use of AI into her lessons for older students. But in some aspects of the class, she also bans it altogether so that her students can focus on thinking for themselves.

"I understand very well that it's tempting to use AI," she said.

There are also other problems with AI in education. According to the Brookings study, students with basic skills can use AI to deepen their learning and progress faster.

But for children with gaps in their knowledge, they tend to adopt AI's errors, outsource their thinking and then fall even further behind. In this way, AI can exacerbate preexisting inequalities.

The PISA study notes that children from more affluent backgrounds often have a better start, and AI can widen that gap.

This is called the Matthew effect — the name comes from the biblical verse Matthew 25:29, "for unto everyone that hath shall be given." It basically means that early success in learning leads to better progress in the future, while early struggles equal a growing lag over time.

In the age of AI, teachers have become more motivated to challenge students to think independently and to consider their own personal autonomy.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Hinn, who also supervises the school newspaper, noted: "I always tell everyone, you can use AI but the feeling of having written an article with your own pen is spectacular.".

Sources indicate that both teachers also stress the idea of personal autonomy and responsibility. They believe this affects the students, especially because when they sit exams, they aren't allowed to use any aids or AI. And if they aren't able to solve their own problems, they will fail.

It's during exam time that the students really find out if they can solve those math, English or science problems by themselves.

Müller said one of her students recently confessed they were upset after a poor exam result. "He felt he simply couldn't think for himself anymore because of AI," she said.

This article was originally written in German.

After his Â£30m move from Manchester City in 2025, McAtee endured a difficult start to life at the City Ground.

Yet he played a key role as Forest toppled City and the returning Anderson before the international break for their first home win of the season.

Nine starts in Forest's run to the Europa League semi-finals could not hide a campaign of frustration.

It was supposed to be a platform after captaining England Under-21s to Euro 2025 victory, but he played only 289 minutes in the league.

The 24-year-old has already tripled those minutes this season after becoming a key player for Glasner, starting every top-flight game.

It followed the manager suggesting in the summer that McAtee could replace Anderson following his Â£116m move to City - something which left McAtee unsure.

"When I first came in and [Glasner] put me in the [number] six [role] on the second day in my head I was like: 'oh, he's not seeing me in his prepares, I'm playing deeper'," he said at Forest's training ground.

"My confidence is growing, but not fully there yet, but I think we're on our way.

"I thought I had it in my locker, but I never thought he would actually try it out with me in pre-season.

"I think Ibra [Sangare] was injured at the time so I was thinking, I'm just going in for Ibra. But then as pre-season got on and I was playing there I felt more comfortable.".

Forest fan impressed by 'surprise' player who stepped into Elliot Anderson's shoes.

It was evidence of McAtee's work after he worked throughout the summer to return for pre-season.

He trained with former Plymouth, Leeds and Ipswich midfielder David Norris, now a personal trainer, and put on 2.5kg of muscle while losing 1kg of fat.

Weight sessions followed fitness work in the morning, which is what prompted Glasner to credit his summer of work.

It has been revealed that the relationship with Glasner has been crucial. The Forest boss has offered clarity and calmness to a squad which endured the chaos last season.

A post-match inquest following the 2-0 defeat by Brentford sparked the right response from the squad, after a start which has left them 16th in the league.

After McAtee failed to find consistency and rhythm last season, Glasner promised him he would be afforded time and the benefit of the doubt if he had a poor game.

Industry observers note that "I think [last season] was a me problem. I was struggling to get my chance," he stated, having used a psychologist before the start of pre-season.

Industry observers note that "I've never really had a season like that, I was always in and out. It was frustrating, but as frustrating as it was, it was a good lesson.

"As I saw my confidence kept going worse and worse and worse. As I've watched clips of me, I can tell when I was going a little bit under.

"This year, if I make a pass and I lose it, it won't bother me as much because I've been through that.".

McAtee has always had supporters at the City Ground. All four managers were impressed by his training levels last season, but he was always under pressure to deliver when given a brief chance.

Forest technical director George Syrianos has also championed the calls internally for McAtee.

It has allowed McAtee - whose brother John plays for Bolton - to feel the faith, having learned from previous difficulties, with England on his mind.

He is eager to make the step up to Tuchel's senior side, and has supporters at the Football Association.

He prioritised playing for the U21s at Euro 2025 - captaining them to victory - over going to the Club World Cup with City, and underlined his determination to represent his country to manager Pep Guardiola and director of football Txiki Begiristain at the time.

Now, under Glasner, after a difficult first season, McAtee has that platform with Euro 2028 a realistic target.

"At this moment I need to have a good year for me to maybe be in with the chance of getting picked, but the competition in the position I'm playing is so high," he said.

"If I could add some goals, some stats, it could put me within a chance to be around that circle. The competition is very elite at the moment, but that's the aim, that's the goal.".

James McAtee had two previous spells on loan at Sheffield United.

Against City, he was moved further forward, with Ryan Yates coming in to add more bodies in midfield.

But the stats back up McAtee's improvement and he compares favourably to others.

Sources indicate that he has made the most final-third passes for Forest (151) and has played the joint-most through balls with Morgan Gibbs-White (five). His 426 passes are behind only Murillo's 501, and he has created 18 chances - six short of Gibbs-White.

McAtee is only 29m behind Gibbs-White, having carried the ball 1,180m this season, but has made the most carries with 109 and has won possession back 63 times - winning 53% of his ground duels, indicating he has developed more of a mean streak in his game.

He has comfortably outperformed Everton's James Garner - one of his rivals for a place in the England squad - creating more chances, making more forward passes, winning more defensive duels and making more successful tackles.

McAtee has also made more recoveries, successful tackles, passes and clearances than Crystal Palace's Adam Wharton.

Now, having gone under the radar this season, come the next international break in March, Tuchel may not be able to ignore him.

"I'm seeing this as a different side of myself, I'm so much more confident on the pitch, I'm so much more comfortable," adds McAtee. "It's like two different players.".

⏱️ ~15 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Taylor Swift and Jack Antonoff and Ludwig Göransson began their long march to widely predicted Oscar glory on Wednesday, Nov.
  • “I Knew It, I Knew You,’’ which Swift and Antonoff wrote for Toy Story 5, won song – animated film.
  • It has been revealed that göransson’s score for The Odyssey won score – feature film.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Taylor Swift and Jack Antonoff and Ludwig Göransson began their long march to widely predicted Oscar glory on Wednesday, Nov. 18 when the 17th annual Hollywood Music in Media Awards (HMMA) were presented at the Avalon in Hollywood, Calif.

“I Knew It, I Knew You,’’ which Swift and Antonoff wrote for Toy Story 5, won song – animated film. Swift accepted her first HMMA in a prerecorded video shown during the ceremony. (Swift was in Nashville on the same night, set to perform on the CMA Awards, where “I Knew It, I Knew You” was nominated for single of the year.).

It has been revealed that göransson’s score for The Odyssey won score – feature film. Last year, Göransson won two HMMAs for his work on Sinners and went on to win both the Oscar and Golden Globe for best original score.This wasGöransson’s eighth HMMA; his second in this category.

It has been revealed that legendary songwriter Diane Warren won her third HMMA for “One Right Here” from Maserati: The Brothers. She performed the song during the show joined by Tia Simon and Joshua Wentz. “One Right Here” was recorded by Andrea Bocelli and Jennifer Hudson for the upcoming film.

Lana Del Rey and David Arnold won song – video game (console & PC) for “First Light” from 007 First Light, which they co-wrote and Del Rey performed.

The Rise of the Red Hot Chili Peppers: Our Brother, Hillel, directed by Ben Feldman, won music documentary – special program.

Linda Perry performed her song “What Lies With You” from Linda Perry: Let It Die Here and won for song – documentary film. The Decemberists frontman Colin Meloy performed his nominated song “The Better Part of Bravery” from Wildwood, and Brother Verses Brother stars Ethan Gold and Ari Gold performed their nominated song “Brothers Keep Goin’ Anyway” from the film.

In a recent development, the Isley Brothers, joined by David Kushner and Pink Beard, opened the ceremony with a performance of Warren’s song “By Any Means” from the film of the same name. The video for “By Any Means,” directed by Fran Strine, won the HMMA for music video.

Michael star Jaafar Jackson won his first HMMA for song – onscreen performance (film) for “Bad.” Daveed Diggs won song – onscreen performance – TV show/limited series for “Raise Him Up” from The Boys, which he co-wrote with composer Christopher Lennertz.

La Bola Negra composer Raül Refree won for both score – independent film and song – independent film for “La Nieve.” The song was co-written by Guitarricadelafuente, Raül Refree, and Lucas Duran, and performed by Guitarricadelafuente.

It has been revealed that behemoth! won music-themed film, biopic or musical, and its director Tony Gilroy was honored for his commitment to the art of film music in Los Angeles.

The award for score – short film [live action]) went to The Seventh Turn composer Michael Wandmacher, who transformed Evanescence frontwoman Amy Lee‘s voice into a full multi-instrumental film score.

Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced received two HMMAs. Composers Brian Tyler and Stephen Lukach won score – video game (console & PC), and Ubisoft Music won soundtrack album.

The HMMAs honor composers, songwriters, music supervisors and artists for outstanding contributions to music in film, television, video games, and other visual media. Here’s the full list of nominations for the 2026 Hollywood Music in Media Awards, with winners marked:.
