#36091. Tech Report: I Will Never Stop Playing ‘Grand Theft Auto’

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1390 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 WIRED ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: I Will Never Stop Playing ‘Grand Theft Auto’

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1390 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I knew GTA was something special even before my mom punched me in the face.
  • She’s not much of a gamer, so the controls on the PS5 version of Grand Theft Auto Online are a bit of a mystery to her.
  • Industry observers note that GTA has been a part of my life since I was way too young to be playing it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I knew GTA was something special even before my mom punched me in the face.

This was an accident. She’s not much of a gamer, so the controls on the PS5 version of Grand Theft Auto Online are a bit of a mystery to her. She pressed the circle button, and her in-game character swung a giant punch that caught my character right in the head. Blood splattered. My mom cried out. My brother and I howled with laughter. She’d only been playing for a couple of hours, and she was already punching her kids. What a violent nightmare these games were.

Industry observers note that GTA has been a part of my life since I was way too young to be playing it. My brother and I, aged 9 and 11-ish, discovered Grand Theft Auto 3 at a cool cousin’s house. We’d sit there, enraptured, cackling like gremlins and passing the controller back and forth every time one of us got WASTED. I remember wondering if video games could ever get more realistic.

Recent findings suggest that flash forward a couple of decades, and Grand Theft Auto VI releases on Thursday, a game poised to be the most lifelike, expansive title in the series—maybe in all of gaming. (The game apparently has a system for tracking your empathy.) It also has a real chance of becoming perhaps the highest-grossing entertainment property of all time.

People are very excited about this thing, so much so that there’s been hand-wringing about workplace productivity dropping because some 12.5 million people are taking time off to play the game. (It’s me; I am part of the problem. Please don’t tell my boss.).

Does that feel like too much hype for a video game? Not to me. Not when Grand Theft Auto has always been such a presence at very pivotal points in my life. It’s been much more than a flashy violence simulator.

My brother and I were the target demographic for these games. Vaguely inspired by gangster shoot-em-ups like Scarface, the GTA games have long been vehicles for male power fantasies. We got into them because you could run around and blow stuff up. Be chaotic. It was a good place to do that in, rather than, you know, the real world.

Sources indicate that we also weren’t always that friendly when we entered adulthood. Lots of siblings aren’t all that close, especially as adults. When you live far away for long enough, phone calls and occasional visits can only do so much. The distance can be hard to close.

Industry observers note that that really changed for us during the Covid-19 pandemic. My brother and I lived hundreds of miles apart. As it did for many people, playing games became a way to stay connected. The best conversations usually happen while doing something like chatting on a long drive, going on a walk, or hanging out at the beach. You couldn’t really do that in the endless Zoom parties Covid unleashed upon the world, where you’d all sit there, talking one at a time, not quite making eye contact on the screen.

Grand Theft Auto Online proved to be a rich environment for finding those kinds of activities. I think it’s the closest anything has ever gotten to feeling like an actual metaverse, where you can do just about whatever you want.

If you’ve played GTAO, you’ve probably rage-quit after getting bombed by an adolescent fighter jet pilot dressed like the prison Joker for the eighth time. That’s fair. But my brother and I usually made the mostly unconscious decision not to fight back. We’d just … hang out. Drive around. Watch the sunset. Spend hours in the in-game nightclubs, listening to real-life musicians play hour-long sets made specifically for the game. We’d go to the stores and curate outfits that felt snazzy.

Sources indicate that really, we are just playing dolls. GTA is a sandbox, after all, and it became the perfect space to mess around without worrying about any real stakes.

It has been revealed that “We were brothers before, sure, but we weren’t like adult friends,” my brother told me when I asked him about GTA. “This gave us a way to spend time together and really learn more about what each other’s personality really is.”.

In a recent development, we’ve made friends with a group in Australia who shared our approach, just hanging out in this vast virtual world and having casual conversations with the people around us. We’ve managed to convince our parents, who have never played games before, to join us. My mom—who once took our Nintendo 64 cartridge of GoldenEye 007 and smashed it with a hammer because she thought video games would make us violent—now runs around with us in GTA Online, pummeling tailgaters’ cars with a baseball bat. Despite the distance, we can spend time together in something that feels close to a real-life hang, one where we accidentally get smacked with the bat sometimes too.

Sources indicate that it’s been a blast, and all that time spent in this virtual world starts to bleed over into the real world. I’ve sought out real-life shows of artists on the soundtrack. Sometimes an outfit would feel snazzy enough that we’d later try to replicate it in real life. One of our in-game characters got killed by a mountain lion on the same night a deer in the front yard was eviscerated by a real-life cougar.

In a recent development, rockstar seems to be acutely aware of this phenomenon. (Maybe not the mountain lion bit.) What GTA does better than any other game series is spread out into the real world in surprising ways. You can see it in their marketing. Rockstar has given exclusive game clips to shows like South Park. The Weather Channel previewed the game’s advanced weather systems. Older games used music to supplement the game, but now GTA VI has become a major marketing tool for artists like Sza and Justice. Having songs in the game can garner thousands of latest listeners.

Recent findings suggest that “When this moment reaches enough critical mass, I think we will see this whole new model for entertainment more broadly,” says Joost van Dreunen, a video game industry analyst. “It's a little bit more of an orchestrated effort between what we play and watch and listen to and attend and connect with and share things online.”.

GTA VI has excited many people for a long time. It stands to be the single greatest-selling entertainment product of all time. It’s why role-play servers are still running and populated 13 years after GTA V was released. It’s why Rockstar has invested in this creator-driven community and detailed numerous content-capture features coming to the new title. Van Dreunen says GTA VI is more like an “operating system” than a standard video game—a hub for people to build off of in unprecedented ways.

Like its longtime player base, the game is also bound to be much more grown up. The worlds of the GTA games have always been critical satires of certain periods. GTA VI seems keenly aware of how it is meeting the present, so much so that alt-right grifters are dedicated to calling it woke.

It has been revealed that “GTA used to be a very much male-dominated audience,” van Dreunen states. “It's very white in so many ways. It's a privileged lens on a lot of these social cultural challenges.”.

Industry observers note that with GTA VI, all these die-hard gamers are about to start a long story where they spend half the time playing as Lucia, a Latina woman who is one of two main characters. (One of my Australian GTAO friends told me she’s very excited that Lucia is in the game, as that means better tattoos and clothing style options for female players.).

Industry observers note that “The fans are being examined as much as GTA has historically put a lens on everything else,” van Dreunen says. “They’re pointing a mirror and critiquing the gamer audience itself.”.

According to recent reports, this feels like a particularly good time to be doing that. My brother and I, plus a billion other people, can’t wait to dive in. Lots of us will probably never be able to put it down.

On this day in space! Nov. 16, 1974: The giant Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico broadcasts humanity's 1st interstellar message

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (658 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • 16, 1974, humans sent their first message to the stars in an attempt to contact extraterrestrials.
  • They did this using what was then the largest radio telescope in the world, located at the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico.
  • It also included figures of a human, the solar system and the Arecibo telescope.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, on Nov. 16, 1974, humans sent their first message to the stars in an attempt to contact extraterrestrials.

They did this using what was then the largest radio telescope in the world, located at the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico. A group of scientists led by Frank Drake and Carl Sagan sent their message to the M13 star cluster. The message was written in binary code and contained information about human DNA.

It also included figures of a human, the solar system and the Arecibo telescope. The idea was that if any aliens were to receive the signal and figure out how to decode it, they would know where it came from. Because M13 is 25,000 light-years away, it will take 25,000 years for any M13 aliens to hear our message — if they are even out there.

According to recent reports, the Arecibo message is only one of several messages intended for extraterrestrials, but this signal sent from Puerto Rico in 1974 was humanity's first intentional olive branch to the stars. At the time, it was the most powerful broadcast ever beamed into space, according to the SETI Institute.

It has been revealed that "The broadcast was particularly powerful because it used Arecibo's megawatt transmitter attached to its 305 meter antenna," SETI wrote of the broadcast in a project over. "The emission was equivalent to a 20 trillion watt omnidirectional broadcast, and would be detectable by a SETI experiment just about anywhere in the galaxy, assuming a receiving antenna similar in size to Arecibo's.".

The message was designed by astronomy professor Frank Drake of Cornell University (who also developed the famed Drake Equation for alien life), as well as Cornnell graduate students Richard Isaacman and Linda May, and Arecibo staff member James Walker, with input from astronomer Carl Sagan and others, according to Cornell University.

The message included 1,679 bits that were arranged in 73 lines of 23 characters per line, all prime numbers, with the broadcast lasting less than 3 minutes, according to SETI.

As of 2026, the message should have traveled about 52 light-years (1 light-year is the distance light travels in a year), with 24,948 light-years to go before reaching star cluster M13.

It has been revealed that the Arecibo message may have been the first message of its kind, but it wasn't the last. We have also included messages on several spacecraft, such as Pioneer and Voyager. NASA and Paul McCartney also beamed a performance of "Across the Universe" in 2008.

Sources indicate that want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube.

On this day in space! Nov. 15, 1988: The 300-foot Green Bank Telescope collapses suddenly, leaving a huge pile of wreckage in West Virginia.

Hanneke Weitering is a multimedia journalist in the Pacific Northwest reporting on the future of aviation at FutureFlight.aero and Aviation International News and was previously the Editor for Spaceflight and Astronomy news here at Space.com. As an editor with over 10 years of experience in science journalism she has previously written for Scholastic Classroom Magazines, MedPage Today and The Joint Institute for Computational Sciences at Oak Ridge National Laboratory. After studying physics at the University of Tennessee in her hometown of Knoxville, she earned her graduate degree in Science, Health and Environmental Reporting (SHERP) from New York University. Hanneke joined the Space.com team in 2016 as a staff writer and producer, covering topics including spaceflight and astronomy. She presently lives in Seattle, home of the Space Needle, with her cat and two snakes. In her spare time, Hanneke enjoys exploring the Rocky Mountains, basking in nature and looking for dark skies to gaze at the cosmos.

#36086. ‘Never Go Backwards, Just Make Things Bigger and Better’: How Paul O’Neill Chartered Trans-Siberian Orchestra’s Journey Ahead

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 12m • 📚 Deep Dive (2444 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Billboard ↗ Open Full Page

‘Never Go Backwards, Just Make Things Bigger and Better’: How Paul O’Neill Chartered Trans-Siberian Orchestra’s Journey Ahead

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2444 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Billboard

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • When Trans-Siberian Orchestra turned 20 back in 2016, the troupe’s enduring success was as surprising to founder Paul O’Neill as anyone in or outside of the camp.
  • Industry observers note that “I would love to say that we planned for it to resonate like this, but it was just pure luck,” acknowledged O’Neill, who passed away the following year at the age of 61.
  • “Normally you have five or six other platinum albums, then you take on Christmas,” O’Neill noted.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When Trans-Siberian Orchestra turned 20 back in 2016, the troupe’s enduring success was as surprising to founder Paul O’Neill as anyone in or outside of the camp.

Industry observers note that “I would love to say that we planned for it to resonate like this, but it was just pure luck,” acknowledged O’Neill, who passed away the following year at the age of 61. And that it was an endeavor almost entirely based around the Christmas holiday made it seem even less likely. Related Underscores Is First Transgender Woman Nominated for Best Dance/Electronic Recording Grammy Ella Langley Becomes First Act to Earn Top Two of TouchTunes Frontline Chart El Coyote Earns Third Regional Mexican Airplay No. 1 With 'Ranchero Enamorado' Explore Trans-Siberian Orchestra See latest videos, charts and news.

See latest videos, charts and news.

“Normally you have five or six other platinum albums, then you take on Christmas,” O’Neill noted. “Of course, we took it on first and the rest of the year on later. It’s all worked out.”.

That’s certainly an understatement for TSO, which celebrates the 30th anniversary of its triple-platinum debut album, Christmas Eve and Other Stories, this year with its annual, two-tech giant concert tour opening Nov. 19 in Green Bay, Wisc., and Council Bluffs, Iowa. The 97 performances through Dec. 30 will again feature the soundtrack and narration from The Ghosts of Christmas Eve, TSO’s 1999 made-for-TV film, and other material amidst the usual fusillade of arena-filling special effects and pyrotechnics, with two indicates a day at most stops.

During the past three decades TSO has released six studio albums — four platinum or better, three Christmas-themed  — and an EP, along with the multi-platinum singles “Christmas Eve/Sarajevo 12/24” and “Christmas Cannon.” The 2005 track “Wizards in Winter” also hit platinum, and a fan’s synchronized home display soundtracked by the tune was turned into an ad campaign for Miller Lite.

Since 1999, meanwhile, the tours have sold more than 20 million tickets, grossing more than $1 billion. This year, too, TSO will continue its practice of donating $1 from each ticket sold to local charities.

According to recent reports, “One of the first things Paul taught us was, ‘Listen, just try to make great art, try to make the best of this as we can, and with a little bit of luck everything will fall into place,'” Al Pitrelli, TSO’s musical director and guitarist with the West company, tells Billboard via phone. “Boy, those words come true every time we hit the stage. His integrity and work ethic carried us through 21 years of touring and 25 years of recording, and with his family at the helm and everybody’s dedication to this, there’s really no end in sight.”.

In a recent development, “Christmas Eve/Sarajevo 12/24” was the opening shot for TSO. Inspired by the true story of cellist Vedran Smallovic, who would play Christmas carols atop rubble in war-torn Sarajevo even amidst attacks during the Bosnian War, it was written by O’Neill, Jon Oliva and Robert Kinkel and first recorded by Savatage — a band O’Neill began producing and writing for in 1987 — for its 1995 concept album Dead Winter Dead. TSO drummer Jeff Plate, who had recently joined Savatage, remembers that “there was a lot of conversation about whether this song should even be on the record. Was it too weird having a Christmas song on this rock/metal record? But it was awesome. There was really something special to it.”.

It was released as the album’s second single and climbed both the Hot Mainstream Rock Tracks and Hot Adult Contemporary Track charts, with enough radio to play to give O’Neill an idea.

“It became an instant holiday hit,” Plate says. “This was the vehicle for Paul to create the Trans-Siberian Orchestra.”.

Pitrelli, who was part of Savatage along with Plate and Oliva at the time, joined the “Sarajevo” brain trust in creating songs for Christmas Eve and Other Stories, based on a narrative created by O’Neill.

“We’d get together at Paul’s apartment in Newly introduced York City,” he indicates, “and literally sit around what we called the kitchen table with four Korg Mi1s, whatever keyboards we had available, a couple guitars, a couple practice amps, an ashtray and a bunch of cassette recorders. Paul would say, ‘Here’s an idea, who’s got a musical thought?’ and we’d throw ideas around and Paul would go, ‘Ooh, I like that. Let’s run with that’ and press record on the tape recorder,’ get it down and then, ‘OK, who’s got something else?’ and move on to the next song.

According to recent reports, “It was three months of having fun, because what did it matter? It had never been done before, so we weren’t up against it. We were just being artists from four different backgrounds, collaborating, throwing out our respective ideas. And Paul saw the significant picture and picked and chose what he thought was appropriate.”.

The formally trained Pitrelli claims the quartet did share a fondness for progressive rock and its blending of classical and rock motifs that they felt was well-suited to the Orchestra component of the Trans-Siberian sound.

Recent findings suggest that “I grew up listening to a lot of Yes, Emerson, Lake & Palmer, King Crimson and (Pink) Floyd, Queen,” he states. “So the orchestral piece made sense in the context of soundtrack and story; it wasn’t far-fetched at all. We just toughened it up and made it a little more aggressive…and then brought in the holiday component and wove those themes and songs into what we were doing.

“We put it all together and took it into the studio. Two or three months later (October 1996) we had a record out, and then it sold three million copies that first year. So it was like, ‘Alright, we’re a band. This is cool, and it’s working. People like it!'”.

Adam Lind, who was managing Savatage with Krebs Communications and now works with both acts for Night Castle Management Inc., adds that, “The part that surprised me was Paul’s accompanying story and poetry. I didn’t know it was coming ’til it was dropped on our desks…The music, for me, was so out of the ordinary and so powerful that it shocked me when I heard it. I wasn’t at all surprised that people loved it…(but) we didn’t know how vital and influential it would be.”.

Lind notes, also, that, “Atlantic (Records) as a whole didn’t understand it, but they were great supporters like Jason Flom, who tirelessly worked every angle and pulled every favor to get it in front of people, and all of a sudden it had momentum.”.

It has been revealed that TSO released one more album, the double-platinum Christmas Attic in 1998, before taking the next step to become a road act. “We were making records, selling millions of copies, but I almost felt like I was in the Steely Dan of Christmas,” Pitrelli remembers. And there was certainly skepticism about the idea of TSO as a live band — though those were allayed when the seven initial theater shows in 1999 all sold out.

It has been revealed that “I think Paul’s presentation and vision of the live show was the secret sauce,” Lind says. “Knowing Paul, it was in his brain the whole time. One of his many talents with being a producer with an ability to see greatness in other people. Over two years he put his friends from his years in the industry together, just as he did for the first record.”.

Pitrelli remembers sitting with O’Neill in the dressing room of Philadelphia’s Tower Theatre on opening night, still not certain about what lay ahead. “It was like, ‘I don’t understand; who bought all these tickets, dude?’ Who is this audience,” the guitarist notes. “When the houselights went down and the curtain dropped, I looked out at the audience and right in front of me was this older couple, grandparents wearing crocheted seaters, and right next to them was a dude wearing a Slayer hoodie. Welcome to the demographic of TSO; that was the weirdest thing that had ever happened to me, musically.”.

Plate recalls being “so nervous” at the same show, and looking at the crowd before to see “metalhead kids, long hair and black T-shirts, and then there were families and children. And in the front row was this gentleman with a tuxedo on his wife had a beautiful red dress. I thought, ‘Omigod, these people are here to see an orchestra!’ But it was just magic; the band, the story, everything just clicked.

It has been revealed that “And at the end of the show the band took a bow and the man in the tuxedo gave me a high five. It set the tone for all these years later.”.

In a recent development, TSO rapidly grew into the two-company, arena-filling endeavor it is now, hauling 325 tons of equipment around in 38 trucks, with a crew of 250. And rest assured it’s definitely a concern where size matters, and bigger is better.

According to recent reports, “Every year we always say the same thing — ‘How the heck are we going to beat this?'” O’Neill, a self-confessed “pyro whore,” noted during 2016. “It’s a good problem to be having, and it forces us to come up with something latest, something different. We know all the special effects companies. They all know that if they invent great special effects that’s insanely expensive there is one band that is dumb enough to buy it, and that’s us. It’s just worth it.”.

TSO tour director Elliot Saltzman claims that “What would Paul do?” has remained a credo since O’Neill’s passing. “His theory was to never go backwards, just make things bigger and better,” Saltzman explains. Planning for each year’s tour begins in earnest during March, starting with drawings from longtime production designer Bryan Hartley, and continues with several meetings in Las Vegas to consider lighting, effects and other aspects of the show — an exacting, detailed dialogue that Saltzman says runs even through rehearsals that begin during October in Omaha, Neb.

“The idea is to really capture the audience and say, ‘Yes, maybe it’s a story you’ve heard before, but the way it’s portrayed this year is different, and that makes it fresh and fresh,” says Saltzman, who also oversees the logistics of transporting band crew and stage from an evening performance and having it ready for a matinee in another city the following day. “We have basically three or four different stories we use, so we’ve got to increase the excitement every year and give them a reason to come and hear them again.

“I talk to people and read comments — ‘This is my 28th show,’ ‘This is my 90th show…and this was the best one yet!’ So we seem to be doing it right.”.

O’Neill considered the live edition of The Ghosts of Christmas Eve, which first aired on the Fox Family Channel, to be “a significant experiment” when TSO presented it on stage in 2015. “We weren’t sure it was going to work,” he acknowledged the following year. “But it worked so well we decided to do it again this year.” Its combination of relative brevity and a “greatest hits” nature of songs from the first two TSO albums has turned it into a something of a staple; this year’s tour marks Ghosts’ eight performance, and fourth in the past five years.

“People love this show,” drummer Plate says. “It’s always worked whenever we’ve done it. It moves along swiftly. The TV special is on all sorts of channels during the holiday season and has become kind of a tradition, too, so it all works hand in hand.”.

According to recent reports, pitrelli adds that, “The story is so universal and has such lovely, happy ending. I just think people love it, myself included. And we listen to the comments; I know our management team is constantly scouring the Internet for feedback, and people say the same thing — ‘We love the story, and they made it even better than the previous year.’ So it’s back by popular demand, and I’m OK with that.”.

More surprises, meanwhile, come during the rest of the show, drawing from the other TSO albums, both Christmas and secular, and in recent years even including songs from Savatage, which itself began touring again last year with Pitrelli, Plate and other members who are also part of TSO.

Industry observers note that “It’s not the same band, but they’re certainly related (because) the same people wrote (TSO)’ songs,” Pitrelli states. And Plate explains that, “If you listen to that band you can hear and see hints of what Paul O’Neill was thinking, and how it turned into (TSO). So doing some (Savatage) songs just fits.”.

Sources indicate that that TSO will go on for the foreseeable future is a given. But there are also hopes that the group’s catalog will expand at some point.

The last TSO album Letters From the Labyrinth, came out during 2015, and TSO did perform a new song, “Christmas Carousels” — an expansion of a track from 2004’s The Lost Christmas Eve — during 2022. Meanwhile, O’Neill left behind several unrecorded projects that he spoke freely about — among them: Romanov: When Kings Must Whisper, about the 1917 Russian Revolution; The Path of the Fairytale Moon; and an expanded, rewritten version of Savatage’s 1990 concept album Gutter Ballet.

“Paul left us a huge body of unfinished work we need to get to,” Pitrelli says, “but we got blind-sided when we lost him and we’re still kind of licking our wounds a little bit. It’s just extremely daunting. There’s always talk about that, but (touring) has become such a full-time job throughout the year that we’re just trying to move forward on this and make sure it’s great.”.

Industry observers note that plate claims he’d like to see one of those works finished and would also like to see TSO try another spring tour, which it did during 2010-2012 in North America and Europe. “It’s difficult in this day and age to go out on tour, no matter who you are,” he acknowledges, “and Trans-Siberian Orchestra is not a small group. If we don’t have the luxury of the holiday it changes things, so it may not be feasible. But it would be nice if we could.”.

#36085. Can a 'coalition of the willing' create momentum for a fossil fuel phaseout?

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1061 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

Can a 'coalition of the willing' create momentum for a fossil fuel phaseout?

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1061 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that this time last year, as negotiations at the UN COP climate summit in Brazil entered crunch time, there was hope that governments would agree on a clear roadmap for phasing out oil, gas and coal.
  • But instead, after opposition from oil-producing states such as Russia and Saudi Arabia, the conference wrapped up with a watered-down final agreement that did not explicitly mention fossil fuels.
  • As a compromise, summit host Brazil offered to produce a "voluntary" roadmap.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that this time last year, as negotiations at the UN COP climate summit in Brazil entered crunch time, there was hope that governments would agree on a clear roadmap for phasing out oil, gas and coal. More than 80 countries backed the idea.

But instead, after opposition from oil-producing states such as Russia and Saudi Arabia, the conference wrapped up with a watered-down final agreement that did not explicitly mention fossil fuels.

As a compromise, summit host Brazil offered to produce a "voluntary" roadmap. At the same time, a group of 57 countries frustrated with the deadlock at the consensus-based UN talks decided to form a "coalition of the willing" to accelerate the fossil fuel exit outside the COP framework.

They held their own summit in April in Santa Marta, Colombia — the first such conference to specifically focus on implementing the transition away from fossil fuels (referred to as TAFF).

Co-hosted by Colombia and the Netherlands, the Santa Marta conference brought together countries including Canada, Norway, Brazil, Nigeria, Mexico, Australia and Germany, as well as highly climate-vulnerable states such as Vanuatu.

The idea was for governments to start developing national roadmaps and working out how to restructure their financial and trade systems to wean themselves off polluting energy sources — an incredibly complicated undertaking, particularly for developing countries dependent on revenue from fossil fuel exports.

Part of their discussions focused on cutting subsidies for oil, coal and gas, as well as supporting people whose livelihoods rely on the fossil fuel industry to find upcoming forms of income.

A little over six months on from the Santa Marta meeting, representatives from almost 200 countries are holding talks in Antalya, Turkey, as part of the latest UN climate conference.

Recent findings suggest that countries agreed for the first time in 2023 to transition away from fossil fuels — the main driver behind rising global temperatures. But summits since then have failed to pin down how to implement that pledge.

It's not yet clear whether the Santa Marta coalition will influence ambition at this year's COP.

"I think it's more of a long-term game," said Chetna Hareesh Kumar, a climate policy analyst at the Berlin-based research organization NewClimate Institute.

Sources indicate that she states it's too soon to expect the coalition to have an influence on the negotiations but adds that that could change at future COPs. The grouping could bring more nations on board if, for example, it indicates it can be truly inclusive, address the needs of different types of countries and show that a transition is feasible.

One role the group is playing, according to Alexandra Scott, a senior climate diplomacy adviser at Italian climate change think tank ECCO, is "keeping up the political momentum," and showing "that there is this huge group of countries who really want to accelerate this transition away from fossil fuels.".

She says it's also building an invaluable "cadre of knowledge" on how to develop national TAFF looks and deal with barriers individual countries face — like how to secure funding for the infrastructure investments needed for the energy transition.

The Santa Marta group is "really answering a lot of the questions that countries have always had on how on earth do we even start to transition our whole economy off fossil fuels?" Scott mentioned.

This expertise being shared and tested in practice can show what such a transformation could look like and the knowledge brought into COP, added Scott.

Sources indicate that since the Santa Marta conference, Germany, France and the Netherlands have released national aims to phase out fossil fuels. While the plans contain no fresh commitments, experts see them as a positive first step.

Kumar notes more countries could announce similar aims just ahead of the second TAFF summit in Tuvalu next year. Finland presented its TAFF roadmap in the first week of COP, but analysts do not expect many more countries to follow suit soon.

Another potential boost that could get momentum going is Brazil's recently published global roadmap to transition away from fossil fuels, promised at last year's COP.

The nearly 200-page document seeks to serve as a toolkit for countries shifting from fossil fuels to renewable energy, such as wind and solar. It envisages countries making a phased transition between 2028 and 2033.

The aim, Ana Toni, CEO of last year's COP, told AP, is to break down the transition into "smaller actionable solutions" and help countries make practical progress.

The roadmap suggests measures tailored to each country's circumstances, including dependence on fossil fuel and financial capacities. "Levers" it proposes include reducing fossil fuel subsidies, expanding renewable energy and cutting methane emissions.

Recent findings suggest that kumar called it a "customizable" approach that allows every country to take action, regardless of its situation. "The question really is now what countries do with it and how much momentum they can generate," she added.

This year's climate change summit in Turkey — taking place after a series of deadly heat waves in Europe and a glacier collapse in Nepal that killed more than 1,400 people — isn't expected to result in any big announcements about fossil fuels.

It has been revealed that global renewable energy capacity has surged in recent years, making up a third of the world's power generation for the first time in 2025. But many countries still rely on coal, oil and gas.

A database compiled by the German environmental organization Urgewald highlights that most oil and gas companies worldwide, among them QatarEnergy, Saudi Aramco and Russia's Gazprom, are exploring or developing latest reserves.

Meanwhile, subsidies for fossil fuels amount to around $920 billion (around €830 billion) per year, according to data from the OECD, but that number is falling.

Industry observers note that one issue Turkey is pushing at the COP conference is electrification. It's calling on countries to endorse the goal of 35% of final energy consumption coming from electricity by 2035 — up from around 20% today.

The pledge has drawn criticism from some circles, though, for leaving open whether that additional electricity needs to come from clean sources.

Ideally, Kumar stated, electrification would be powered by renewables and tied to a goal of phasing out polluting fossil fuels.

"If something like that could make it to the final text, that would be a really good sign for momentum.".

#36084. Latest Update: Nubia Redmagic 12 Pro Review: Furiously Fast but Flawed

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1220 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 WIRED ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: Nubia Redmagic 12 Pro Review: Furiously Fast but Flawed

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1220 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, mobile gamers don’t have many dedicated gaming smartphones to choose from, so Nubia’s Redmagic series stands out.
  • Industry observers note that sadly, Nubia has followed every other phone manufacturer this year, offering minimal iterative improvements while jacking up the price significantly.
  • According to recent reports, the Nubia Redmagic 12 Pro sports the same boxy design as its predecessors, just a teeny bit slimmer and lighter.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, mobile gamers don’t have many dedicated gaming smartphones to choose from, so Nubia’s Redmagic series stands out. This massive, boxy phone offers cutting-edge performance, long battery life, and a large display. You also get touch-sensitive shoulder buttons, RGB lighting, and gaming-focused software features.

Industry observers note that sadly, Nubia has followed every other phone manufacturer this year, offering minimal iterative improvements while jacking up the price significantly. While this series has always been a clear bargain for gamers seeking the best chipset, it’s harder to swallow the compromises lurking here (camera, software, revision commitment) when the price starts at $949.

According to recent reports, the Nubia Redmagic 12 Pro sports the same boxy design as its predecessors, just a teeny bit slimmer and lighter. I’m a fan of the translucent industrial aesthetic and RGB lighting, but it’s not something I really want in my everyday phone. I had exactly the same issues with the 12 Pro as I had with the 10 Pro I reviewed two years ago. It’s very big, so you really feel it in your pocket, and it can be awkward to handle, especially when you’re trying to scroll one-handed. It’s also the most slippery phone ever. Every time I put it down, the 12 Pro slowly starts to slide away.

The substantial positive of this design is that it feels great in landscape orientation for gaming. The thick frame is easy to hold. There are touch-sensitive shoulder buttons on the top edge, and Nubia has a dedicated Magic Key for gaming mode, though you can customize it to launch the camera. This used to be a switch, but is now a red button. It’s still flanked by the round power button. Sadly, there’s no headphone port.

It’s refreshing not to have a camera bump on the back, though this inevitably adds to the slipperiness, and this glass sandwich quickly gets covered in finger smudges. Nubia has toned down the lighting a little, but you can still customize it for all sorts of activities. There’s a powerful cooling fan inside, with two vents to expel hot air, but the 12 Pro still somehow scores an IP68/69 rating for dust and water resistance.

The 6.85-inch OLED display is completely uninterrupted, with no notch or cutout camera to break it up. There’s an effective fingerprint sensor at the bottom and a less effective selfie camera under the top of the screen. The screen can hit a 185-Hz refresh rate, but only a handful of games actually support it. Most of the time you’ll be capped at 120 Hz. It supports HDR with 5,000-nit local peak brightness for highlights, but overall brightness is capped at 1,900 nits. Overall, it’s a lovely display, and a pleasure to play games or watch movies on. The Dolby Atmos–certified stereo speakers are decent for a phone.

Perhaps the biggest enticement is Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 chipset, paired with Redmagic’s RedCore R5 chipset and 12 or 16 GB of RAM. You won’t find a faster Android phone right now, and the Redmagic 12 Pro can even give the iPhone 18 Pro a run for its money. Benchmark scores topped the Android charts, above phones like Samsung’s Galaxy S26 Ultra.

I had no problems playing Asphalt Legends and Wuthering Waves with settings cranked to the max. I also tried PUBG Mobile, one of the titles that can support that 185-Hz refresh rate, and it was smooth sailing. The 12 Pro keeps its cool, even after an hour or so of challenging gaming. Aside from the fan and vapor chamber for cooling, Nubia added dual-loop liquid cooling. You do get some fan noise and thermal throttling, but the 12 Pro has enough grunt to satisfy even the most hardcore of gamers.

In a recent development, to keep you gaming for longer, the 12 Pro boasts an enormous 8,400-mAh battery. Even with hours of gaming, I made it to the end of every day with something left in the tank. With careful use, you could easily push this phone to two days. There’s no charger in the box, but it supports up to 80-watt wired or wireless charging if you spring for a Redmagic charger. It took me an hour and 17 minutes to charge it from dead, but you can hit around 50 percent in half an hour. Sadly, it doesn’t support Qi2 magnets, so you’ll need a flat wireless charging pad.

Sources indicate that to get top-notch performance at this price, you’ll have to accept several compromises. Let’s start with the camera. While the main 50-megapixel camera is quite good, and there’s a 50-megapixel ultrawide, the flat design doesn’t leave room for a telephoto lens, so you can only get 2X zoom by cropping. The main camera will satisfy folks who only snap the odd photo, and it does well in most conditions. The ultrawide is fine for group shots, but its smaller sensor means performance suffers in low light. The 16-megapixel front-facing camera is hidden under the screen, and it’s fine for video calls or well-lit selfies, though shots often look a bit muddy.

According to recent reports, the real problem with the 12 Pro’s camera is the processing. Use the terrible portrait mode or zoom in too far and you’ll see how badly it handles image processing. Nubia lacks Google’s expertise in this space, so a camera system that sounds similar on paper produces far worse photos in reality. Nubia’s colors often look a bit off, it really struggles with mixed lighting, and shots tend to be noisy or oversharpened. Video recording is quite good with the main camera, but stabilization was a little poor in some of the videos I shot.

Another massive turnoff with the 12 Pro is the software. Redmagic OS 12 sits atop Android 17, and it’s mostly OK, though I wish Chinese manufacturers didn’t feel the need to imitate things like Apple’s Liquid Glass. The interface also has some bad translations. What’s worse is the prevalence of absolute junk bloatware and the subpar upgrade commitment. Nubia is only promising two years of platform updates and three years of security software updates in the US (five years in the UK).

Our best Android phones guide includes many more well-rounded options than the 12 Pro. You can even buy a Pixel 11 Pro XL on sale for the same price right now. But the 12 Pro is all about gaming, and to that end, it offers the best performance-and-screen combo you can get today. Whether the gaming features, cooling tech, and overall style add enough value depends on you. That same chipset will roll into more phones soon, and most of them will have a better camera and longer software support, but they’re likely to be more expensive, like the forthcoming Motorola Signature 27 at $1,600.

Industry observers note that for buyers in the US, check your carrier bands. The 12 Pro should be fine with T-Mobile and its associated MVNOs, but it may not work well, or at all, with some other carriers. It also doesn’t support eSIM, so you need a physical SIM card. The 12-GB RAM and 256-GB storage model is $949; upgrading to 16 GB and 512 GB costs $1,049, and the 1-TB model is $1,199.

NASA’s Parker Solar Probe discovers a hidden pattern in the Sun’s chaotic magnetic fields

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (793 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Turbulence is all around us, from milk swirling into a cup of coffee to powerful storms churning through the atmosphere and oceans.
  • It has been revealed that unlike the air and water on Earth, much of the matter in space consists of electrically charged particles in a state (known as the plasma state).
  • Scientists have long struggled to explain how turbulence develops under these conditions and how energy is distributed among its constantly changing fluctuations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Turbulence is all around us, from milk swirling into a cup of coffee to powerful storms churning through the atmosphere and oceans. But turbulence also occurs throughout space, where it behaves in ways that scientists are still struggling to understand.

It has been revealed that unlike the air and water on Earth, much of the matter in space consists of electrically charged particles in a state (known as the plasma state). These particles interact strongly with magnetic and electric fields, creating turbulence that is fundamentally different from what we experience on Earth. Space plasma is also so thinly spread that particles rarely collide with one another, making its behavior even more unusual.

Scientists have long struggled to explain how turbulence develops under these conditions and how energy is distributed among its constantly changing fluctuations. Now, an international research team has uncovered a surprising clue: hidden within the seemingly random motion of space plasma is a distinct magnetic pattern that reverses direction at very small scales.

The discovery, published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters, reveals a previously unobserved phenomenon that could improve our understanding of the solar wind and the turbulent conditions that influence space weather.

NASA's Parker Solar Probe Reveals a Hidden Magnetic Reversal.

Researchers from the Technische Universität Braunschweig and the University of Tokyo, working with Tohoku University, Kyushu University, Osaka University, and other international institutions, identified the phenomenon using observations from NASA's Parker Solar Probe.

The collaboration brought together scientists from ten countries, including researchers at the Institute of Theoretical Physics at Technische Universität Braunschweig.

By analyzing highly precise measurements of magnetic fields and particles, the team discovered that turbulent magnetic fields reverse their direction of rotation at a particular range of wavelengths. This marks the first direct observation of such a reversal in space turbulence.

Even more surprisingly, the reversal becomes more pronounced and shifts toward longer wavelengths as the solar wind travels farther from the Sun.

The change occurs at a critical boundary where the behavior of plasma shifts from the collective movement of a flowing fluid to the dynamics of individual particles. This connection suggests that the magnetic reversal may provide an crucial new way to understand how turbulence operates across different physical scales.

Finding Order in the Chaos of Space Turbulence.

At larger scales, plasma moves much like a fluid. Swirling structures called vortices and electromagnetic waves create increasingly complex fluctuations, producing the turbulent conditions found throughout space.

Although these movements appear random, the researchers discovered that the rotation of the magnetic fields follows a consistent pattern.

When viewed along a direction pointing outward from the Sun, magnetic fields at larger scales tend to rotate counterclockwise. At much smaller scales, however, the preferred rotation switches to clockwise.

This reversal occurs precisely where plasma stops behaving primarily like a fluid and begins exhibiting behavior governed by individual particles.

The finding is particularly striking because it reveals a clear, organized feature within a system otherwise dominated by seemingly unpredictable fluctuations.

"We see a clear structure in the spectrum, even though the turbulence represents unstructured motions," says Dr. Masatomi Iizawa (TU Braunschweig), the study's first author.

Dr. Yokoi (University. of Tokyo) emphasizes the broader importance of the discovery, stating, "The results are of great significance for both plasma physics and astrophysics.".

Why the Discovery Matters for Solar Storms and Space Weather.

Although the magnetic reversal occurs at extremely small scales, understanding it could have far-reaching consequences for space physics.

Plasma turbulence is a major feature of many environments throughout the universe, including Earth's magnetosphere, the solar wind, regions affected by solar eruptions, interplanetary space, and the disks of material surrounding astronomical objects known as accretion disks.

It also influences the shock waves and clouds of magnetic material that travel through interplanetary space following eruptions on the Sun.

These disturbances can play an important role in geomagnetic storms, making plasma turbulence a critical factor in efforts to predict space weather.

It has been revealed that by showing how an organized magnetic pattern emerges as turbulent plasma transitions from fluid behavior to particle behavior, the new research provides an key piece of a longstanding physics puzzle. The findings could ultimately help scientists better understand the complex processes that govern the solar wind and improve the physical models used to forecast geomagnetic storms.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The top 10 European strikers of the 21st century.

Classic number nines, penalty-box poachers, troublesome targetmen and tireless all-rounders.

There is no one-size fits all when it comes to determining great strikers, but they do all share a common trait - a ruthlessness in front of goal.

This week, however, we put the power in your hands to decide the best European frontmen of the 21st century.

Tens of thousands of you voted on the 20-man shortlist drawn up by our panel.

We then asked European football experts Guillem Balague, Julien Laurens and Raphael Honigstein to discuss your choices on the Euro Leagues podcast.

So from 10-1, here are the best European strikers this century - as voted for by you.

Top 10 European Strikers of the Century - Part One.

Karim Benzema comes in at number 10, the former Lyon and Real Madrid frontman's closest challengers coming from across the continent in the shape of Raul, Robin van Persie, Michael Owen and Miroslav Klose.

Industry observers note that laurens: "From a young age you could see he was something special. I know it was difficult at the beginning at Real Madrid, but in the post-Cristiano era he carried that team, wore the armband and won massive titles and trophies by being decisive in big moments. Like I used to say 'Karim the dream'.".

According to recent reports, honigstein: "The selflessness, the ability to work for the team. A sense of elegance and humility on the pitch, which is unusual in a goalscorer. I think he is unusual in that list. I think not many will define themselves through their teamwork and assists as much as their goals, but he was that player.".

Ruud van Nistelrooy edges Benzema, with whom he briefly overlapped at Real Madrid - the Dutchman teed up the Frenchman and scored himself in their only La Liga appearance together, before he left for Hamburg in January 2010 following injury problems.

The former PSV striker's most consistent spell, of course, came at Manchester United, where he scored 150 goals.

According to recent reports, honigstein: "He is the nicest guy but he never came across that way on the pitch. Typical trait of a striker, he would kill to score the goal. I think anyone who has grown up with him scoring goals, for United especially, must have a soft spot for him because he was a phenomenal poacher.".

Laurens: "He was a strong player physically, and despite the lack of pace the awareness in the box was just very special even with all the injuries.".

It has been revealed that zlatan Ibrahimovic slots in at eight, comfortably clear of Van Nistelrooy and Benzema. The Swede netted more than 500 times in a career that spanned Malmo, Ajax, Juventus, both Milans, Barcelona, Paris St-Germain, Manchester United and LA Galaxy.

It has been revealed that balague: "He was a big-game player and that explains the league titles with PSG. Scoring four goals against England, the overhead kick. The personality thing has put him one or two places in this list, saying 'I am great, I am the best'. If you keep saying you're great it makes people stop and think.".

Laurens: "The mentality of really believing he was the best and nobody was better than him, apart from maybe Brazilian Ronaldo, who was his idol growing up, and he would watch videos of him and try to replicate in his council estate. If you watch a highlight reel of his best goals he was incredible.".

Sources indicate that honigstein: "What makes him unique among the strikers is his technique, You could see elements of martial arts in his goals. No-one scores goals like that.".

The first Englishman on the list, although the third to have represented Manchester United - it's the Old Trafford outfit's record goalscorer, Wayne Rooney.

Honigstein: "I don't think there is anyone who would've watched English football at that time [early in his career] and not been enthralled by his game. The only downside is the combination of injuries and not the most professional lifestyle meant he did not fulfil his potential. He could've been Messi.".

In a recent development, balague: "What could have been, yes. He was the national team's record scorer too before Harry Kane took it. I find him to deserve this place as he had to adapt to a lot of strikers and he did it well. He had the ability to link up and score. He was very intelligent.".

It has been revealed that laurens: "He is the most street footballer England has ever seen. There's no rules, that kind of anger you saw on the pitch. I don't think people in England realise how good he was.".

Sources indicate that what does becoming the all-time World Cup top goalscorer get you? Sixth place on the best European strikers this century list. The Real Madrid forward, 27, just misses out on the top five.

Sources indicate that laurens: "Maybe if we do this ranking again in a few years he will be higher. I would have had him top five, for sure. He has scored more than 400 goals. I don't think Messi and Ronaldo had scored that many at that age, so he's ahead. I don't know if he will play for as long as them but he hasn't done much wrong in his career.".

Recent findings suggest that balague: "This list has to do what you feel about the player, not science - 22 goals in 22 appearances in World Cups and [Euro] Championships. He should be at least top three because of that. Great stats, but we're not in love with him.".

Sources indicate that honigstein: "I don't think there is a forward that is as good as footballer as him in 2026. On that basis alone he should be higher, but people when they vote have other things in their head. The only way to win everyone over is to score more goals and win more World Cups for France, which I think is possible.".

Industry observers note that there was little between Mbappe and Erling Haaland, but it is Manchester City's prolific Norwegian who slips in at fifth. The 26-year-old has already scored more than 300 club goals and has a staggering 68 in 61 games for his country.

Balague: "Mbappe should be higher than him. Haaland scored 52 goals in 53 games [in 2022-23], that is astonishing, but he's gone 11 finals without scoring. We're talking about the best. We're talking about what we see at the moment and what we see is someone who is calculated but in a more charming way. An ability to score we haven't seen in a while; power, ability to finish. He is not world class to the level of others.".

Recent findings suggest that honigstein: "I don't think it's fair to judge him on just that. They [Manchester City] won the Champions League when he was there. When Haaland arrived with Pep Guardiola, they found a way to do it. What makes him unique is the physical attributes and the pace. To have both is unique. He can sprint like a 100m sprinter. Is he the fifth best striker of the 21st Century? I don't think he's that far behind.".

Interesting, this, because Robert Lewandowski is well clear of Haaland in fourth, but the leap from the Polish forward to the top three is massive - more than 10,000 votes.

The 38-year-old is still chipping away for Chicago Fire in Major League Soccer, having been a reliably ruthless assassin for Barcelona, Bayern and Dortmund.

Sources indicate that honigstein: "He used to play basketball, judo, handball - his father wanted him to have a wholesome education. You could see his completeness that he had as a centre-forward. Nothing in his game was extraordinary but in terms of ticking all the boxes, none come close to him.".

Balague: "He mentioned he learned to be an elite striker when he forgot what he had just done, like a fish. Mistakes he had in his head affected his performance. One day he just continued like it didn't matter.".

Laurens: "He won the Ballon d'Or in Covid, it won't be on his mantlepiece but we all know it was his.".

Fresh from his Ballon d'Or triumph, England's record goalscorer and appearance maker rides into the top three on the back of 61 goals in 51 outings for Bayern Munich last season.

Kane left the Premier League three years ago with the second-most goals ever in the competition, and is also Tottenham's all-time record scorer.

According to recent reports, honigstein: "Third place, at least. He is doing incredible things. At 33, still not quite at his peak. I don't think he relies on his pace, physicality, it's all about intelligence, technique. I don't think there's anyone in the game that strikes a ball as well as him right now. I don't think any player comes close that we've talked about so far in overall work-rate, defending, helping the team, making tackles in your box in the 90th minute when you're 3-0 up because he's that kind of guy. He is humble and a superb human being.".

Recent findings suggest that laurens: "What I love about Kane, from a young age, a lot of this list you just knew the trajectory would be all the way to the top. Kane was not like that. It could have been very different for him. Nobody at 17 would've stated he was going to win the Ballon d'Or. Nobody believed in him like the others. Kane had a very different journey.".

Runner-up Thierry Henry is the only striker in the top six who is retired. A World Cup and Euros winner with France, Henry won titles with Arsenal - where he scored 228 goals - and a Champions League with Barcelona.

In a recent development, honigstein: "During his time, I don't think there was a player like him in the Premier League. The way he played football was stylish, elegant, but there was almost a kind of a romantic connection between him and the ball. I don't think there was anyone near that kind of level of technique and, for want of a better word, va-va-voom he exuded. That just made for amazing viewing.".

Industry observers note that laurens: "For me as a fellow Parisien, he's a very special player, a very special man. A career that has been incredible from a young age. It's that season in the Premier League - 24 goals, 20 assists in 38 games - not even Kane or Benzema or Cristiano, OK, Messi is different, but they haven't done that and yet he did it.

"There are still some people who undervalue him and underappreciate him and the monster that he was on the football pitch. He had it all. The pace, the style, the elegance, the technique, the mentality, the goals, the aura, the charisma. Just everything you wanted if you were to build a striker. One of the greatest football brains ever.".

Industry observers note that of course, at number one, it's the man chasing the 1,000-goal dream. Cristiano Ronaldo may have retired from Portugal duty with 146 notches on his strike chart but the quest goes on at Al-Nassr.

The 41-year-old's evolution from tricky winger to prolific frontman has taken him from Sporting to Manchester United, twice, Real Madrid, Juventus and now Saudi Arabia.

Industry observers note that balague: "He's the best striker in history. His numbers are incredible. He won't stop until he gets to 1,000. He is somebody who is special. We know his background, how he wanted to be Ballon d'Or winner at 12 and didn't stop until he got there. He ran up the mountains of Funchal with weights in his ankles and snuck into the gym when it was closed to get the physique he wanted.".

Sources indicate that laurens: "Always in the right place at the right time. The instinct. He was born with a gift, like all in this list. But you still have to work hard. Nobody will ever reach those levels again. 1,000 goals for club and country will never be done again, I think.".

Industry observers note that honigstein: "Peak Ronaldo for me was Gareth Bale scoring and him looking very unhappy. I don't think there will be any dispute about him being the greatest. Somebody who has done it all, won it all, and he's still going for the love of it.".

Satellites now outnumber the visible stars above most towns

💡 Key Takeaways
  • More than 700 satellites are crossing the sky over an average mid-latitude town at any moment of the night, outnumbering in many cases the stars visible to the naked eye.
  • According to recent reports, that's based on an analysis of the trajectories of the 15,833 active satellites that at the moment circle the planet in low Earth orbit below an altitude of 1,200 miles (2,000 kilometers).
  • Recent findings suggest that the results were published as a non-peer-reviewed study conducted by engineering firm Accu Components, and is based on satellite monitoring data from the U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

More than 700 satellites are crossing the sky over an average mid-latitude town at any moment of the night, outnumbering in many cases the stars visible to the naked eye.

According to recent reports, that's based on an analysis of the trajectories of the 15,833 active satellites that at the moment circle the planet in low Earth orbit below an altitude of 1,200 miles (2,000 kilometers). Analyzing data from Oct. 12 and 18 this year, researchers found that with a completely unobstructed horizon, 710 satellites were crossing the sky in every single moment of the night above an average U.K. town.

Recent findings suggest that the results were published as a non-peer-reviewed study conducted by engineering firm Accu Components, and is based on satellite monitoring data from the U.S. Space Force available through the public website CelesTrak. Although the researchers specifically focused on the U.K., they say that such heavy satellite traffic flows above most of Europe, the U.S. and other mid-latitude regions, especially between 40 and 50 degrees north or south.

Sources indicate that "Most Starlink satellites orbit at around 53 degrees to the equator, so the satellites bunch up over the mid-latitudes. These worldwide figures are approximate, based on a global grid over a single day," Accu Components spokesperson told Space.com in an email. "Skies near the equator are the quietest, with around 490 satellites.".

Not all of those satellites are visible to the naked eye, the researchers noted in a statement. Because satellites unlike stars don't produce their own light, they must be illuminated by the sun, while the ground below has already sunk into darkness, to be visible. According to the study, an average of 105 satellites out of those 710 were catching light as they zoomed overhead, shining as bright as stars.

It has been revealed that the spokesperson said that the actual number of visible satellites varies drastically throughout the night. During the hours after dusk and before dawn, a much greater number of satellites can be seen, while in the middle of the night most no longer catch any light.

Sources indicate that "For a typical U.K. town, around 300 satellites are catching the sunlight in the first hour or so after dark," the spokesperson remarked. "That falls to fewer than 20 around midnight, then climbs back to around 300 before dawn.".

Industry observers note that for comparison, as little as a few dozen stars are visible to the naked eye in the dead of the night above large, light-polluted megalopolis such as London or New York, according to OwnStarMap. In suburban areas and smaller towns, that number grows to a few hundred. To get to a few thousand visible stars, one must retreat into remote countryside or isolated mountain ranges.

Recent findings suggest that the number of satellites orbiting Earth has grown steeply in the past decade, especially since Elon Musk’s SpaceX began launching its internet-beaming Starlink constellation. Satellite companies blueprint to launch hundreds of thousands, possibly millions of satellites in the coming decades. If those visions come to pass, the number of passing satellites will vastly outgrow that of stars almost anywhere in the world. The trend especially concerns astronomers who fear the impacts on humankind’s ability to study the Universe.

It has been revealed that satellites crossing the view of ground-based telescopes leave streaks in astronomical images and increase the overall brightness of the sky through the light they reflect down towards Earth. Gradually, even the most powerful telescopes could lose their ability to see the distant stars and galaxies that hold the answers to key questions about the history of the universe.

According to recent reports, the study found that throughout the night, an average U.K. town sees 12,891 different satellites passing overhead.

In a recent development, tereza is a London-based science and technology journalist, aspiring fiction writer and amateur gymnast. She worked as a reporter at the Engineering and Technology magazine, freelanced for a range of publications including Live Science, Space.com, Professional Engineering, Via Satellite and Space News and served as a maternity cover science editor at the European Space Agency.

Germany dominated neighbor and historic rival the Netherlands in their Nations League quarterfinal match-up at Berlin's Olympic Stadium on Monday evening.

It was the team's sixth game under head coach Jürgen Klopp and the 50th ever between the two sides.

In a recent development, germany's 5-0 shellacking of the Oranje was their most lopsided victory since 1959, when they won 7-0. In all, Germany have now won 19 of those matches, the Netherlands have won 12, and 18 ended in a draw.

Speaking to German broadcaster ARD after the game, attacking midfielder Florian Wirtz — who scored twice in the fixture — said: "We hope that we can make it fun for the fans. It was definitely fun for us, especially in the second half.".

Despite the loss, Xavi Hernandez's Dutch side will reach the final eight alongside Germany.

Prior to the match, Klopp had made it clear that he and his team were approaching Monday's showdown as a final after having lost to Greece 1-0 in his first home game in the job on September 27.

By night's end, Derry Scherhant and Nico Schlotterbeck each scored once and Brajan Gruda scored once and added two assists on top of Wirtz's double.

Klopp has been high on Wirtz, who has come under fire for not delivering at Liverpool since his arrival there in June 2025, and his bet seems to be paying off with the 23-year-old now scoring four goals in his last four games for Germany.

"We don't care who we play. We want to play attacking football. We want to score goals and dominate the opponent. And I think we did that perfectly," said Wirtz on Monday evening before adding: "We want to keep going next year. We want to get better. I think we've taken some great steps in our development as a team.".

A group of five EU member states, including Germany, have entered talks over a scheme to send rejected asylum seekers to Rwanda.

The plan to set up so-called return hubs in a non-EU country had been announced by the group — which also includes Austria, the Netherlands, Greece and Denmark — had first been announced back in September.

Tesla has earmarked some €3 billion ($3.3 billion) to expand its factory in Germany, near to Berlin.

The Grünheide complex will be expanded to start producing the electric car firm's driverless Cybercabs, with output expected to eventually reach 1 million units.

The Elon Musk-owned company noted construction would begin in 2027, with the first Cybercabs rolling off the line in 2029.

"With this, we are laying the foundations for the world's most technologically advanced Tesla factory here in Grünheide," Tesla said.

Germany coach Jürgen Klopp has joined the chorus of football figures critical of FIFA President Gianni Infantino. But with time running out, there are few who seem willing to run against him.

Matt Pearson on our sports desk breaks down where the power struggle presently stands, with the deadline for candiates just a matter of hours away now.

Lawmakers in the state parliament in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania have voted in Manuela Schwesig for another term as state premier.

The 52-year-old has been in the role since 2017 and is heading into a third term.

The vote was a secret ballot, but it can still be assumed who voted and how.

She received 39 of the 68 votes cast in the chamber, exactly as many as commanded by Schwesig's three-party coaliton of her Social Democrats (29), the ecologist Greens (5), and the socialist Left Party (5).

While Söder's comments in Munich focused in particular on the policy the coalition in Berlin had not delivered, Merz initiatlly focused on talking up the efficacy of his federal coalition.

"We are aware of the situation. We know that we now need to deliver. And we also know that we face difficult talks within the coalition. But I would also say from the experiences of the last weeks that there are solutions to the problems which we have in Germany," Merz noted.

Merz remarked that in the 18 months since last year's election, the coalition "has already successfully implemented many things, not 'set them into motion' as people like to say, but actually implemented.".

He noted a total of 17 bills going through the second and third reading process in the lower house of parliament, the Bundestag, last week, "including the most comprehensive reforms of our intelligence and security services that we have ever done in [post-war] Germany.".

Among others, he thanked Bavarian Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt, a senior member of the Bavarian CSU sister party to Merz's own conservative CDU, for his contribution to this.

Merz also touted the support given to CSU politician Ilse Aigner, not just from his CDU but from the Social Democrat coalition partners and the Greens, to become the next president, calling her a person who would "represent our country very well at home and abroad.".

After hailing these accomplishments, Merz then turned to electricity tax cuts, saying he anticipated talks on the matter on Tuesday that would be "very short.".

He said that over the weekend, coalition leaders had revisited the figures, and now believed they would be able to "completely" reduce electricity taxes to the minimum European levels in 2027 "also for private households.".

Bavarian state premier Markus Söder has appeared with Friedrich Merz at a press conference during the chancellor's trip to Munich.

It seems Söder, Merz and the CDU/CSU believe they have unfinished business after the budget was finalized in the Bundestag late last week.

Merz had pledged in the run-up to the decision to provide a reduction in electricity tax for all, but the final agreement did not include this step, with the coalition partners the Social Democrats (SPD) saying it was not adequately costed.

Söder noted he and Merz had discussed "backup for the coming days," for Berlin and for a "collective stance, that is really, really important.".

He remarked the coming days were about "demonstrating credibility in politics," seemingly in reference to Merz's promise that the coalition did not ultimately deliver.

Industry observers note that "That's why it's really vital to us that we do indeed bring about the reduction in electricity tax," Söder said. "This is important for businesses. It would be a relief for citizens. But it's also a matter of credibility and it's written in the coalition agreement.".

Söder stated that as to the question of "where the money comes from, with a €560 billion (roughly $615 billion) budget, with €200 billion in new debt, nobody can tell me there's no potential within the budgeting process.".

A festive piece of merchandise on the right-wing populist Alternative for Germany (AfD) "fan shop" website has upset some religious leaders in Germany.

Called a "chocolate Nicholas," it appears to depict a semblance of Saint Nicholas in bishop's regalia and the party's colors and holding a book with "AfD" written on the cover where a Bible might be in more traditional iconography.

The Bishop of Essen, Franz-Josef Overbeck, was highly critical of the promotion in Monday's edition of the Bild newspaper.

In a recent development, "The AfD is appropriating Christian symbols for party campaigning," Overbeck mentioned. "Showing the holy Nicholas in a blue coat with mitre, staff and the gospel with an AfD logo is not in order.".

Overbeck acknowledged that other organizations like football clubs would sell chocolate Christmas figurines in club colors, but he mentioned they would tend to refrain from including overtly Christian symbols when doing so.

Bild quoted an AfD spokesman as saying that as a "liberal-conservative party that clearly associates itself with Christian values," the item fit "particularly well" with the party image.

The main German protestant church group EKD's cultural representative, Johann Hinrich Claussen, said the offer showed the AfD had "no understanding of traditions and no respect" for Christianity.

He described the action as "embarrassing and revealing," and said that Christianity was "supra-partisan.".

According to recent reports, "The AfD knows little about what is holy to Christians. Otherwise, it would be aware that Bishop Nicholas of Myra, in what today is Demre in Turkey, stood clearly for uniting the occident and the orient. Beyond that, he is the patron saint of rescues at sea," Claussen said.

The partner of deceased Bavarian politician Hubert Aiwanger has noted that anybody is welcome at his funeral this coming Saturday.

Aiwanger was the economy minister in Bavaria's state government as the leader of the junior coalition partners to the center-right CSU.

"Hubert was a man of the people and so it stands to reason that anyone who liked or treaasured him is allowed to come to his funeral," Tanja Schweiger wrote on her Instagram profile overnight.

It has been revealed that she was posting after a requiem in the state capital Munich paying tribute to the leader of the Free Voters (Freie Wähler) party over the weekend. Around 1,100 people attended this ceremony.

Aiwanger died suddenly and unexpectedly on November 4 during a working visit to Berlin, aged 55.

Prosecutors have since mentioned he died of natural causes, after he was found dead in his hotel room.

And there's quite a lot at stake for Jürgen Klopp's team in the last group stage game of the Nations League competition at Berlin's Olympiastadion.

If Germany win, they will qualify for the knockout stages, but a defeat could lead to potential relegation into the second tier of Nations League football.

Klopp was upbeat in the pre-match press conference at the prospect of playing the Netherlands, who he said play "Xavi football," in the image of the skillful Spanish playmaker and World Cup winner coaching the team.

Recent findings suggest that "I've always loved playing against teams like this. For all my coaching career," Klopp said. "When someone says, 'hey they can really play football,' then in my mind the party's already started.".
